Management stated that the manufacturer is now entering a fresh phase of value creation focused on accelerating organic growth and driving operational excellence through technology-enabled solutions. The company reported expansion in its adjusted EBITDA margins and growth in free cash flow, supported by a mix shift toward higher-margin work in digital and nuclear markets. Management indicated that the business remains aligned with durable national security priorities and is positioned to return capital to shareholders through a newly authorized repurchase program while maintaining flexibility for strategic investments.

This approach is allowing us to meet changing customer priorities, which are increasingly focused on speed and solutions, including the use of flexible acquisition pathways to accelerate the transition from prototype to production.

Internally, we are increasingly looking to apply AI and process performance tools in areas like program management, cash generation and back-office operations. Combined with continued process improvements, disciplined contracting and a growing mix of higher-margin work, these actions will help us execute more effectively, drive margin expansion and create additional capacity to invest in the next phase of our growth strategy.

In a recent development, third, we will make investments, deploy capital and manage our portfolio to drive long-term shareholder value. Lastly, we will focus capital deployment on areas that produce the highest risk-adjusted rate of return. Together, these priorities are designed to improve execution and margins in the near term while positioning the portfolio to drive faster growth and long-term shareholder value. Turning to Slide 6. As we have discussed previously, one of the clearest opportunities for growth is in our nuclear business, where Amentum combines deep technical expertise, differentiated customer relationships, global reach and full life cycle capabilities in a market seeing substantial investment. These strengths and the actions we are taking to expand them provide a natural example of how we intend to focus resources in markets where we believe we have compelling competitive advantages and significant growth potential.

Recent findings suggest that the nuclear market continues to gain momentum, driven by growing demand for reliable, secure energy and advancements in next-generation nuclear technologies, including small modular reactors. Customers are pursuing fleet scale reactor deployment, accelerating licensing and regulatory execution, and exploring innovative power solutions to support expanding digital infrastructure needs and national security priorities. As investment accelerates, demand for experienced engineering, licensing and program management solutions continues to grow. In a recent development, together, these investments strengthen our competitive positioning and support our strategy of concentrating resources in markets with attractive long-term growth opportunities. I Put Xiaomi’s 18 Pro Max Camera to the Test and I Love the Results

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xiaomi has taken the wraps off its latest 18 Pro Max Android phone in Paris.
  • The images seen here are taken with the phone’s various built-in camera modes, largely the black and white mode, as I love the dramatic, filmic look it produces.
  • Taken using one of the phone’s built-in color styles, I love the vibrancy in this shot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xiaomi has taken the wraps off its latest 18 Pro Max Android phone in Paris. I’ve had the phone for the past few weeks and have been putting the camera to the test in my beautiful home of Edinburgh, Scotland, as well as on the beautiful (and rainy) streets of Paris. You can check out my review of the phone if you’re keen to hear more about that wild rear screen on the back, but here I wanted to share some of my favorite photos I’ve taken with the phone so far.

The images seen here are taken with the phone’s various built-in camera modes, largely the black and white mode, as I love the dramatic, filmic look it produces. They’re presented either as-shot or with minimal adjustments using the phone’s built-in editing tools.

Taken using one of the phone’s built-in color styles, I love the vibrancy in this shot. The reds really pop, while the wider angle of the main camera emphasizes the tunnel effect of the alleyway, drawing the eye to the person and their dog.

I may be spoiling the rest of the images here by saying that this is my absolute favorite shot I’ve taken, but there we go. I took this using one of the dedicated black-and-white modes, and I think the tones here are perfect. Excellent dynamic range and contrast, and just the right amount of film grain. I positioned the figure between the buildings and had the phone almost on the floor to turn the rain-soaked tiles into a reflective surface to add some drama to this scene. I then applied a wide cinematic crop in post to give it that extra edge. Lovely stuff.

Most of my favorite photos with the phone were taken using the black-and-white mode. It’s no surprise; I shoot in black and white very often on my Leica Q3 43, and I used the monochrome mode for my favorite shots with Xiaomi’s Leitzphone earlier in the year.

The phone captures excellent black-and-white photos at night, too.

Industry observers note that and by exposing for the bright highlights in this scene, I was able to create this stark, moody image of my handsome orange cat, Toulouse. Is he the best cat you’ve ever seen? Of course he is.

Back in color, this UFO that had presumably crash-landed in this Parisian market looks great in this filmic color mode. The oranges and reds pop against the other tones in this scene.

While this quick street portrait is similarly punchy.

In a recent development, I used manual mode here, taking full control over the white balance and exposure settings to achieve the tones I wanted. It’s a great-looking shot with excellent dynamic range. Xiaomi’s phone doesn’t appear to go too hard with its software processing either, meaning that even fine details look quite natural. Other Android phone-makers could take note.

As with the photo of Toulouse the cat, I exposed for the highlights here, forcing the rest of the scene under this bridge into shadow. As a result, it looks moody and dramatic but crucially it also looks exactly as I hoped it would. Many phones would try to artificially lift the shadows here, which would ruin the vibe I was going for.

According to recent reports, I took this with the phone’s telephoto zoom lens, aiming to focus more on the digger as the subject and use the water for reflection. I love how this shot looks, especially in black and white, as the cloud detail behind it is especially noticeable.

While here I used the full wide angle of the main camera in order to create a lot of negative space around the figures, emphasizing the size of the building around them.

That building was Le Grande Arche in Paris and despite it being a miserably cold, wet and cloudy day I think the phone has captured a satisfyingly stark scene here.

I don’t like flying, so I distracted myself on the flight out to Paris by taking photos of things with the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, including this man having a look out of the window.

In a recent development, and this shot of my plane’s wing somewhere above the UK. Again, in black and white. When it looks this good, why would I choose anything else?

And while we’re still in black and white, a particularly friendly pigeon. Hi, friend!

And to round us off, this dude in shades looking at a menu.

I’m genuinely really thrilled with so many of the shots I’ve taken with this phone. The black-and-white mode in particular is spectacular, and I’m looking forward to taking more shots with it over the coming weeks and months.

Editors’ note: Andrew Lanxon’s travel costs to attend Xiaomi’s launch event in Paris were covered by Xiaomi. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Default weather apps are notoriously unreliable, but Google is giving users a chance to help improve things.
  • It has been revealed that A recent patch to the Pixel Weather app introduced a latest “Report current weather” card.
  • “Share the current weather condition,” the card notes, “to improve local forecasts.” If you tap it, you’re given options to indicate whether the current temperature is accurate, warmer, or colder than the app says, and what your current conditions are, with options like cloudy, clear, rain showers, strong thunderstorms, and rain showers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Default weather apps are notoriously unreliable, but Google is giving users a chance to help improve things.

It has been revealed that A recent patch to the Pixel Weather app introduced a latest “Report current weather” card. If the weather you’re experiencing doesn’t match what the app is saying, you can report the discrepancy.

“Share the current weather condition,” the card notes, “to improve local forecasts.” If you tap it, you’re given options to indicate whether the current temperature is accurate, warmer, or colder than the app says, and what your current conditions are, with options like cloudy, clear, rain showers, strong thunderstorms, and rain showers.

Industry observers note that the card also shows what the app currently thinks is happening for you to use as the basis for your report. To find the card, scroll all the way to the bottom of your Pixel Weather app.

Also: Your best Google weather app alternatives (and what I recommend instead).

It has been revealed that google said that it will use your feedback, device location, and “some diagnostic information” to help improve forecasts. Nothing you report will be associated with your Google account. The app doesn’t explain exactly how Google uses your reports, but I’ve reached out to see if the company can offer any details.

Sources indicate that as someone who doesn’t put a ton of faith into default weather apps, I see this as a step in the right direction toward regaining some trust. Even if it’s not yet clear how Google will use the information you send, the goal of improving forecasts is an important one.

Also: I switched to MyRadar as my main Android Auto weather app and don’t regret it.

According to recent reports, A large part of what makes weather apps unreliable is that they lack human insight, and a computer usually can’t grasp the nuance of a local forecast the way a meteorologist would. Experts have also warned of reduced weather forecast accuracy due to recent NOAA budget cuts.

Industry observers note that the Apple Weather app has a similar feature, so it’s good to see Google catch up. I couldn’t find a feature like this for Samsung or any other native app. One of the most popular third-party apps, Weather Underground, does feature a “Report your local weather” prompt. It also gathers information from hundreds of thousands of connected home weather stations.

This new Pixel Weather feature was present on three Pixel phones in my home, so the rollout appears to be widespread.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Roku people may be getting that sinking feeling, as the platform is retiring its classic animated Aquatic Life screensaver.
  • The popular animation featuring realistic aquarium life will be replaced by the Roku City screensaver on Dec.
  • That doesn’t mean all fish-filled options have been flushed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roku people may be getting that sinking feeling, as the platform is retiring its classic animated Aquatic Life screensaver.

The popular animation featuring realistic aquarium life will be replaced by the Roku City screensaver on Dec. 1. Roku City is the platform’s signature purple skyline, featuring rotating digital billboards packed with brand sponsorships and clever pop-culture Easter eggs. (Seattle’s short-spined raccoon, Jimothy, has made an appearance.).

That doesn’t mean all fish-filled options have been flushed. Several third-party Roku wallpaper apps offer a variety of aquarium options to choose from. But if you’re sticking to what Roku itself provides on its streaming boxes, the move away from the aquarium screensaver also means switching to an alternative that’s filled with advertising.

“It seems like this is a way for Roku to convert a popular screensaver into a way to make money, or at least generate more engagement, via the Roku City version,” said CNET Senior Editor Ty Pendlebury, who covers home entertainment options including the Roku streaming boxes.

A Roku representative didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Viewers who miss these specific fish can still watch a YouTube version of Roku’s Aquatic Life screensaver for as long as the organization chooses to keep this nearly 3-minute video on the internet.

The Aquatic Life screensaver loss is a drop in the ocean compared to other changes at the streamer this year. Roku was purchased by Fox for $22 billion in June, which puts the streaming platform under the same ownership as Fox’s Tubi and Fox One channels. That deal is expected to close in 2027.

You might have to wait over a year to get the Samsung Galaxy Watch 10: Samsung will not release any new Galaxy smartwatch in 2027, South Korea’s ET News reported on Sunday.

In an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News. The switch follows other cost-cutting measures that will reduce production of the tech giant’s midrange smartphone lineup while increasing its premium Galaxy S27 offerings.

I am not mad at this decision by Samsung. Annual smartwatch updates are usually iterative anyway. Take Apple, for example. Its Apple Watch Series 10, released in 2024, had the same chip as the Apple Watch Series 11, released a year later. The most recent Apple Watch, the Apple Watch Series 12, has the same battery life as the Apple Watch Series 11. I’d expect Apple to keep its new sensors, which debuted on the Series 12 and Ultra 4, for its Series 13 or Ultra 5 next year.

Samsung’s Galaxy Watch 9, which debuted with a different chip and added a few more hours of battery, had the same bones as the Galaxy Watch 8.

If some of the biggest features on these smartwatches remain the same for a few years, why not change the release schedule to a biannual one?

According to recent reports, also: Galaxy Watch 9 vs. Galaxy Watch 8: I’ve compared both models, here’s my advice.

Some of the most substantial updates that arrive on newly introduced devices like the Galaxy Watch 9 or Apple Watch Series 12 normally arrive through software updates, which end up landing on previous watch generations upon launch as well.

By switching from an annual release cycle to a biannual one, Samsung could drum up more excitement and anticipation between launches, and be able to surprise its customers with more purchase-worthy updates.

Samsung did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

  • Individual features can still be disabled, but they’re scattered across several menus in Settings and Screen Time rather than being consolidated in one place.
  • If your device is not running the newest software, turning off Apple Intelligence all at once only takes a few taps in Settings and doesn’t affect any core iPhone functionality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 26 lets you turn off Apple Intelligence with one toggle. iOS 27 doesn’t. Apple folded its AI settings into a upcoming Siri menu centered on Siri AI and dropped the master switch along the way, so opting out now means working through several parts of Settings. Siri AI’s controls are in the Siri menu, Screen Time can block Writing Tools and image creation, notification summaries have their own switch and each app’s Siri & Search settings control what Siri learns from it. This guide walks through every step in order.

Individual features can still be disabled, but they’re scattered across several menus in Settings and Screen Time rather than being consolidated in one place. Here’s the current map of what can be turned off and where to find each control.

If your device is not running the newest software, turning off Apple Intelligence all at once only takes a few taps in Settings and doesn’t affect any core iPhone functionality. Here’s how to do it on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Sources indicate that you can still disable some of Apple’s AI features if your iPhone is running iOS 27. It just won’t be as easy as tapping the main toggle.

Industry observers note that to disable Siri AI, go to Settings > Siri and toggle off the control. Beware, though, that this will disable your voice assistant entirely, as well as disable conversations in the latest dedicated Siri app and block you from using Apple’s Visual Intelligence. Additionally, your HomePod speakers will not be able to recognize your voice or help with personal content if they’re on the same iCloud account as your iPhone.

Keep reading for how to disable some of the individual Apple AI features.

Since the first Apple Intelligence features rolled out in iOS 18.1, some people have opted out of the newly introduced technology. Tools such as Image Playground, Genmoji and message summaries can use up to 7GB of your device’s internal storage — a sizable chunk, especially if you tend to run against the upper limit of its free space.

In a recent development, even if storage is not an glitch, you just may not be interested in Apple’s set of AI features. A recent CNET survey finds that just 19% of US smartphone owners are choosing to upgrade their devices to take advantage of upcoming AI features. And a recent ZDNET/Aberdeen survey reveals that the majority of US adults say they will not use most AI features, and just 8% would consider paying extra for them. Some AI features are more welcome than others, with 58% of respondents saying using AI for photo editing would be valuable.

Or, honestly, you may not want to deal with features that are creating inaccurate summaries or that can be replicated without Apple Intelligence.

(Earlier iOS 18 updates re-enabled Apple Intelligence automatically even if you had turned it off, but as of iOS 18.4, the setting is honored.).

Recent findings suggest that read more: Did a well-meaning friend send you a message about Apple Intelligence possibly reading your private information? Here’s what’s actually going on.

According to recent reports, I’m not an AI crank — I appreciate features such as notification summaries and the Clean Up tool in the Photos app. And yet, Apple Intelligence is also a work in progress, an evolving set of features that Apple is heavily hyping while gradually developing. I wouldn’t hold it against you if you wanted to not be distracted or feel like you’re doing Apple’s testing for them (that’s what the developer and public betas should be for).

Remember that Apple Intelligence works only on the upcoming iPhone 18 lineup, the iPhone Duo, iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, iPhone 17E, iPhone 16, iPhone 16E, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro or M-series Macs and iPads, plus the newest iPad mini.

If you’re concerned about the storage requirements of Apple Intelligence, you can find out how much the system is using by going to Settings > General > iPhone (or iPad) Storage > iOS (or iPadOS).

See how much space Apple Intelligence is using in Settings. This is what it looks like running iOS 26, but the settings flow is the same.

Sources indicate that note that even after turning off Apple Intelligence, the storage still indicates up in the iOS Storage list. However, I was able to confirm that if the phone’s storage fills up and the system needs that now-inactive space, iOS reclaims what it needs.

Maybe you’re finding some Apple Intelligence features helpful while others are annoying (or just highly amusing). You can turn off specific features in the settings for apps to which they apply.

For example, to disable text summaries in Messages notifications, go to Settings > Apps > Messages and switch off the Summarize Messages option.

Some features are not as app-specific. Writing Tools, which use Apple Intelligence to proof or rewrite text, appear as an option when you select text, regardless of the app. To turn that off, you need to disable Apple Intelligence system-wide.

Sources indicate that also note that nearly every app includes an “Apple Intelligence & Siri” option in Settings, with a Learn from this App option (turned on by default). That applies just to whether Apple Intelligence and Siri can monitor how you use it to make suggestions; it doesn’t affect any particular Apple Intelligence features.

Sources indicate that another option for restricting what Apple Intelligence can do is buried in the Screen Time settings. Screen Time is designed to control which apps and features can run on another device, such as the iPhone used by a child in your household. But it’s also helpful for tracking how much time you’re spending on the device and, in this case, turning off some components of Apple Intelligence.

It has been revealed that turn off selected Apple Intelligence features in the Screen Time settings. This is what the settings look like with iOS 26. It may look different if you are using iOS 27. The settings flow is the same.

If you haven’t upgraded to iOS 27 yet, make a good backup first.

If you aren’t on iOS 27, you can turn off Apple Intelligence with one tap. (You can see what software your iPhone is running by going to Settings > General > About and seeing what iOS version you’re running.).

If you’re on iOS 26 or earlier, here’s how to disable Apple Intelligence. Open Settings (iPhone or iPad) or System Settings (Mac) and choose Apple Intelligence & Siri. Then turn off the Apple Intelligence option. Confirm your choice in the dialog that appears by tapping Turn Off Apple Intelligence.

Turn off Apple Intelligence entirely with one switch if you are running iOS 26 or an earlier software version.

Curiously, the Clean Up tool in Photos sticks around even when Apple Intelligence is turned off, perhaps because the first time you use it the app downloads resources for it and holds onto them.

#85185. Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are Everywhere

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2207 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are Everywhere

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2207 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
  • But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto.
  • Something must be behind all of this, you might think — a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

Microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some complications. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

Something must be behind all of this, you might think — a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these problems, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

Adam Meyers, senior vice president of counteradversary operations at cybersecurity company CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

“This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

One big reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

If it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

Artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a big or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

At the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

Even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should revision. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

According to recent reports, another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

According to recent reports, when I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he said, “it’s bad.”.

As owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He says he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. Latest AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

“You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand stated.

Things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning.

In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers states CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

“Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers said.

It has been revealed that despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

“The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” remarked Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

Recent findings suggest that AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

Sources indicate that the good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

According to recent reports, it still might not be enough, and Significant Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

According to recent reports, and defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella noted at the New York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

Sources indicate that that’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

“There’s effectively this significant backlog of security issues in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” said Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity manufacturer focused on connected devices.

It has been revealed that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

“Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse remarked.

Wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of complications is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with important, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to update so frequently these days.

“It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” said Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

In a recent development, and patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s concerns on Tuesday.

Things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents new problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing issue.

Industry observers note that in the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

Recent findings suggest that big Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

“I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” said Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy claims.

That means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into new software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

The main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

Recent findings suggest that “I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he mentioned. “It will hurt a bit.”.

Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more important than ever.

It has been revealed that “You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers stated. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

But consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a manufacturer isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

We don’t have to put up with it, Barlet claims. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he noted.

Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • With Claude Ship, confirmed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

With Claude Ship, confirmed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

The new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic said, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic noted.

Industry observers note that “It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic remarked it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

According to recent reports, “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz remarked the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

According to recent reports, also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

“But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he stated. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz mentioned he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the tech giant and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he said.

According to recent reports, developer platforms overall are adapting to the newly introduced state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “owners won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Still, that depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the upcoming PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

Sources indicate that anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

BingEx (FLX -1.99%) reported a year-over-year decline in total revenue as competition in the Chinese on-demand delivery market intensified. Management maintained a stable gross margin through optimized merchant acquisition and disciplined spending while significantly expanding the role of artificial intelligence across research and operational functions. The company released a newly introduced service category for everyday assistance and deepened integrations with major platform ecosystems to diversify user acquisition channels. Strategic focus remained on high-value delivery segments and improving the fulfillment capacity of the courier network while executing a multi-million dollar share repurchase program.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to BingEx' 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results Conference Call. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Helen Wu from Piacente Financial Communications. Please go ahead.

Furthermore, throughout the call, we will constantly use the company brand name FlashEx to refer to its publicly listed entity, BingEx Limited. Joining us today from FlashEx senior management are Mr. Adam Xue, Founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; Mr. Hongjian Yu, Co-Founder, Director and Executive President; and Mr. Luke Tang, Chief Financial Officer. I will now turn the call over to Mr. Adam Xue.

In a recent development, peng (Adam) Xue: Thank you, Helen. Hello, everyone, and welcome to FlashEx's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Competition in the on-demand delivery industry remained intense in the third quarter, responded by sharpening our execution and strengthening our differentiated on-demand dedicated courier model. We improved user acquisition efficiency, our merchant mix and fulfillment experience while also expanding into new scenarios and new cities at a measured pace. Doing this work well is what positions FlashEx for long-term growth. Let me start with our overall operations. We fulfilled 62.8 million orders in the third quarter, largely in line with the second quarter and average delivery time held steady at around 25.3 minutes.

According to recent reports, as of the end of the third quarter, our registered users increased to 128 million, registered Flash Riders rose to 3.33 million and our service network expanded to 301 cities. As we keep growing our user base and delivery capacity, we are focusing more on turning these resources into reliable service capabilities while steadily improving operating efficiency. Turning to our financial performance. Total revenues for the third quarter were RMB 929.4 million with a gross margin of 11.2%. Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB 16.1 million. As of the end of the third quarter, our cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 816.4 million, reflecting a healthy financial position.

We also remained committed to enhancing shareholder returns through share repurchases. As of November 23, we had repurchased a total of approximately 4.9 million ADS for an aggregate consideration of approximately USD 13.3 million. Now let me walk through our business in more detail. On the individual user side, we prioritize acquisition efficiency and the conversion of newly introduced users. We concentrated our marketing spend on higher converting channels in the third quarter, lowering new user acquisition cost by more than 30% quarter-over-quarter. First order conversion and order volume from new users both increased. Beyond our own channels, we are also reaching users by integrating our services into the ecosystem of major platforms.

Industry observers note that on the everyday side, total order volume across our 5 lifestyle scenarios grew 3.5% quarter-over-quarter, led by food pickup and parcel pickup. These everyday needs also point us in a clear direction for expanding our lifestyle services. With this in mind, we released our new service, Flash Helper or Flash Assist in the third quarter. It brings the standardized processes and attentive one-on-one service to everyday needs such as waiting in line at restaurants, handling small tasks and moving or carrying items for people. Demand for this kind of assistance has long existed but remains highly fragmented.

Early results show that new users account for high share of Flash Helper orders, making the service an additional channel for expanding our user base and extending user lifetime. We will keep refining the service and use our existing Flash Rider network to explore more services that fit users' daily needs. For users with higher service expectations, we continue to refine our premium delivery service in the third quarter. Premium delivery order volume grew significantly quarter-over-quarter, and the number of new users increased by approximately 37%. This service further diversifies our product tiers, so we can better meet users' varying needs for speed and attention to detail.

On the merchant side, we focused on improving both the quality of our merchant base and our service capabilities while deepening our relationships with existing merchants. We concentrated on raising the quality of newly acquired merchants. To that end, we ran a pilot in 6 cities in northern China, where we optimized resource allocation based on merchants' operating profiles and flexibly adjusted pricing strategies to market conditions in each channel and city, balancing merchant acquisition with ongoing operations. These adjustments are already paying off with gross profit improving in the pilot cities. For our KA business, we moved into a tiered operating model, managing national and regional accounts separately, leveraging the stable high-density order flow from our enterprise clients channels.

Industry observers note that we have built a strong delivery competitive base in core business districts, which in turn is driving newly introduced merchant acquisition and revenue growth in these areas. In the third quarter, average daily order volume from KA merchants grew quarter-over-quarter, and their share of GMV rose to 17.6%. As the quality of merchant business continues to improve, our business has become even more resilient. For entering new cities and new districts, we adopted a more return-driven expansion model. Our existing teams and our partners run this market directly, drawing on the people and experience we already have to get started quickly with lower upfront investment.

In the third quarter, average daily order volume in newly launched cities and districts rose sharply from the second quarter with some areas turning profitable within a short period. These results provide a proven template for future expansion. Going forward, we will replicate the model progressively, tailoring our approach to local market conditions as we enter newly introduced cities. Whether we are serving existing owners or developing new services, reliable fulfillment always comes first. In the third quarter, we strengthened our delivery capacity by starting with the Flash Rider experience. We refined our tiered growth framework for Flash Riders with development paths for those riding regularly, those riding flexibly and those building advanced skills.

In a recent development, we also introduced an owner certification that recognizes Flash Riders for strong service and encourage them to keep improving. As Flash Rider income rose steadily, we saw a higher share of regular active Flash Riders and better fulfillment quality with the perfect order rate climbing further and the complaints continue to fall. Order completion rates also improved year-over-year during peak demand periods and in high-density areas such as holidays and core business districts. A stable, well-supported Flash Rider team ultimately translates into a more reliable experience for our users. Yesterday, we celebrated our ninth annual Flash Rider Day together with Flash Riders across the country.

In a recent development, since we established the day in 2018, we have marked every November 3 by recognizing those who stand out for their professional service and good deeds in the community and by thanking all of our Flash Riders through online and offline events and benefits. Going forward, we will keep investing in safety, skills training, career development and everyday support, creating a better working environment and giving our Flash Riders more room to grow. Our Flash Riders' experience on the road are also helping more users understand the value of FlashEx.

In the third quarter, we built content around real-life Flash Rider stories and expanded our network of around 690 Flash Rider KOLs beyond Beijing to more cities using AI tools to produce and review content more efficiently. For the first time, we also combined a celebrity partnership, holiday timing and a upcoming service in a single campaign, promoting Flash Helper's everyday assistance services during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. Our brand communications focus on showing customers what FlashEx can do for them in specific real-life situations so that every service experience gradually adds up to trust in our brand.

Industry observers note that on the technology front, we continued to put AI into practice to improve efficiency across R&D, customer service and operations. Efficiency gains in these areas increased from 30% in the second quarter to 46% in the third quarter. In R&D, the share of AI-assisted coding exceeded 98%. At the end of September, Super Agent, our self-developed internal development agent, completed its first development tasks end-to-end on its own. Next, we will extend AI further into requirement analysis, testing and release with the goal of shortening development cycles. In customer service, AI has moved beyond standardized Q&A into more open-ended inquiries, now handling close to 90% of cases in core scenarios allow our human agents to concentrate on more complex requests.

In operations, AI tools are increasingly used by our frontline teams. They are gradually moving into a more efficient digital way of working at every level from headquarters to the frontline. Our low-altitude delivery business moved into routine operations in the third quarter. By the end of the quarter, we have built 15 takeoff and landing sites and 24 2-way delivery routes in Hangzhou, covering the city's main districts. Order volume grew 13% quarter-over-quarter. Next, we will focus on 3 areas to further extend the service coverage and capabilities, building a denser network coordinating across channels and partnering with government and other enterprises. Looking ahead, we will focus on improving new owners conversion and optimizing our merchant mix.

Building on our existing capabilities, we will also steadily expand our service scenarios and city network. We will also continue to invest in enhancing the experience of both our Flash Riders and our owners and deepen the application of AI across our business to deliver better service with greater efficiency. For 12 years, FlashEx has built its business around on-demand dedicated courier services. Our focus has always been the same, providing reliable service the user needed at urgent and notable moments. Going forward, with every high-quality delivery and service, we will keep building the trust that the users and merchants place in FlashEx and make that trust the foundation of a long-term sustainable growth. That concludes my remarks.

Sources indicate that now I will turn the call over to our CFO, Luke Tang. Thank you.

According to recent reports, le (Luke) Tang: Thank you, Adam. Hello, everyone. This is Luke. I would like now to walk you through our third quarter 2026 financial results. During the third quarter, our unique on-demand dedicated courier model remained resilient in a competitive market with order volume holding steady quarter-over-quarter. Backed by a disciplined approach to spending and a healthy cash position, we have the flexibility to keep investing in fulfillment quality while exploring new services and use cases. We also remain committed to enhancing shareholder returns through our repurchase program. Before I begin, please note that all numbers are in renminbi and all percentage changes are on year-over-year basis, unless otherwise noted.

Recent findings suggest that our revenues for the third quarter were RMB 929.4 million compared with RMB 1,005.4 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by intensifying market competition. Our cost of revenues for the third quarter was RMB 824.8 million compared with RMB 893.6 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was in line with the decline in revenues. Our gross profit was RMB 104.5 million for the third quarter compared with RMB 111.8 million in the same period of 2025, representing a gross profit margin of 11.2% compared with 11.1% in the same period of 2025. Turning to operating expenses.

In a recent development, our total operating expenses for the third quarter were RMB 93.5 million, representing a decrease of 4.3% from RMB 97.7 million in the same period of 2025. They consisted of RMB 40.3 million in selling and marketing expenses, RMB 36.6 million in general and administrative expenses and RMB 16.6 million in research and development expenses. The decrease in operating expenses was mainly attributable to the reduction in advertising expenses and share-based compensation expenses. Our income from operations was RMB 11.1 million compared with RMB 14.1 million in the same period of 2025. Excluding share-based compensation expenses, our non-GAAP income from operations was RMB 16.1 million for the third quarter compared with RMB 23.7 million in the same period of 2025.

Our net loss was RMB 6.8 million compared with net income of RMB 43.7 million in the same period of 2025. The change was mainly due to an investment loss of RMB 19.7 million in the third quarter compared with investment income of RMB 33.2 million in the same period of 2025. Excluding changes in fair value of long-term investments and share-based compensation expenses, our non-GAAP net loss was RMB 1 million compared with non-GAAP net income of RMB 62.6 million in the same period of 2025. Our cash position remained healthy with cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaling RMB 816.4 million as of the third quarter end.

Sources indicate that we also continue to carry out share repurchases under our existing buyback program. As of November 23, we had repurchased a total of approximately 4.9 million ADS in the open market for an aggregate consideration of approximately USD 13.3 million. This underscores our confidence in the organization's long-term value. As we close out 2026, we remain committed to disciplined execution and to the high-quality service that differentiates us with a distinctive business model and an improving merchant mix and the deeper use of AI across our operations. We are confident in our ability to create sustainable long-term value for our shareholders. That concludes our prepared remarks. We would like to open the floor to your questions. Operator, please go ahead.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] We will now take our first question. This question comes from the line of [indiscernible] from CICC.

It has been revealed that unknown Analyst: This is [indiscernible] from CICC. Actually, two questions on my side. The first one is about margins and financials. We noticed that our gross margins held up well, yet operating margins compressed. Could you please walk us through what drove the pressures on the OpEx side? And on the non-GAAP net loss swing, how much of that is operating versus below the line items? And my second question is about shareholder returns. You still have about half of the buyback authorization remaining. How should we think about the pace of repurchase going forward, particularly given the current earnings trajectory?

It has been revealed that le (Luke) Tang: Thank you, [indiscernible]. I will take your first question and hand over the second one to Adam. Yes, our gross margin held steady this quarter. So the change in operating margin came mainly from operating expenses due to upcoming initiatives we released. During the third quarter, we launched Flash Helper, which helps users do everyday tasks such as waiting in line at restaurants or moving or carrying items. And we promoted it with our first celebrity campaign around the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. So compared with the second quarter, we spent more on marketing to support these debuts. We also kept investing in R&D, especially in AI.

We are already using AI tools to create and review marketing content faster. And over time, we expect them to make our marketing spend more efficient. Going forward, we will remain disciplined on overall spending. On a non-GAAP basis, there was a decrease in the fair value of our short-term investments in the third quarter. Our core business stayed profitable with a non-GAAP income from operations of RMB 16.1 million. Yes, I would like to hand over the second question to Adam.

Peng (Adam) Xue: Okay. Thank you, Luke. And also thank you, [indiscernible], for your question. I will answer the second question. Well, our commitment to creating value for shareholders hasn't changed, and that is what guides our buyback program. In terms of progress, as of November 23, we have bought back about 4.9 million ADS for around USD 13.3 million under our USD 30 million program. Buybacks are one of several ways we return value to shareholders. As for the pace from here, we will stay flexible, taking into account market conditions, operating performance and our funding needs and act when the time is right in compliance with applicable SEC rules. Our balance sheet gives us a solid base for this.

It has been revealed that we ended the quarter with RMB 816.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments. Over the long run, we believe that continuing to strengthen our business, combined with prudent use of share repurchases is the best way to create long-term shareholder value. The buyback program also reflects our confidence in the company's long-term prospects.

Recent findings suggest that operator: That concludes our Q&A session for today. I will now hand back to Helen Wu for closing remarks.

Helen Wu: Thank you once again for joining BingEx' Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update Conference Call today. If you have any further questions, please contact the IR team at BingEx or Piacente Financial Communications. Thank you and have a great day.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

#85177. Can an App Tell When Someone Near You Is Wearing Smart Glasses?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1285 w)

Can an App Tell When Someone Near You Is Wearing Smart Glasses?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1285 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that meta’s smart glasses stay connected to the wearer’s phone over Bluetooth, and that connection is what detector apps look for.
  • It has been revealed that it’s a clever workaround for glasses designed to blend in.
  • Here’s how those apps work, what they reliably catch and what they miss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that meta’s smart glasses stay connected to the wearer’s phone over Bluetooth, and that connection is what detector apps look for. Apps such as Zuckoff scan for the short broadcast signals Bluetooth devices send out and compare them with signals from known smart glasses models. When there’s a match, the app sends an alert. It’s a practical way to learn that a pair is nearby, though the alert can’t confirm whether anyone’s recording, and glasses with Bluetooth switched off won’t appear at all. Here’s how the apps work and how much weight to give an alert.

It has been revealed that it’s a clever workaround for glasses designed to blend in. How useful it is depends on what you want it to tell you: The app can detect that a pair is close by, but not whether it’s recording. Still, that’s more notice than most people get today, especially if they haven’t spotted the glasses’ built-in LED indicator.

Here’s how those apps work, what they reliably catch and what they miss.

According to recent reports, broad concerns over privacy have led to a technical battle. On one side, hardware modifiers are tweaking wearable cameras to make them even harder to spot, often by disabling LED indicators. On the other, developers and privacy-focused coders are launching counter tech to give you a heads-up when a hidden camera walks into the room.

Sources indicate that zuckoff, whose name takes a direct jab at Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, has joined a small ecosystem of apps such as Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner and Nearby Glasses that offer similar functionality — letting you know when someone has smart glasses activated and how close the device is, although they can’t tell you specifically whether someone is actively recording or using AI to pull up information. The apps detect approximate device proximity by sweeping local Bluetooth frequencies to locate vendor IDs, system identifiers and hardware signatures associated with smart glasses.

As Zuckoff’s website notes: “Glasses advertise loudest while powering on, pairing or leaving the case. Once paired to their owner’s phone, they can go quiet, so silence is not proof that nobody is recording, and a detection is not proof that anyone is. Signal strength gives a rough distance and no direction at all.”.

Zuckoff’s developer, Pawel Szydlowski, said he was already working on projects that used Bluetooth to detect nearby devices and discovered the tech could be applied to smart glasses. “It’s just the same technology wrapped in a different paper,” he said in a video chat with CNET.

Recent reports have shown that smart glasses are being used for everything from bullying in schools to viral videos with unwitting subjects who don’t know they’re being recorded.

What drove Szydlowski to actively develop a software detector was seeing social media videos of people wearing smart glasses who recorded pranks or harassed women with pickup lines. None of the targets seemed aware that their content would appear online, which made Szydlowski angry. “There was not even a blur involved to try to censor them, to give them some sort of feeling of privacy,” he stated. “These days, everybody feels entitled to post everything.”.

Since it rolled out in early August, the Zuckoff app has gotten 2,000 sign-ups, and Szydlowski is beta-testing an Android version he hopes to make available on the Google Play Store. The app also has a premium version for $10 a year that can run continuous detection checks in the background when the app isn’t in use.

But a booming ecosystem of DIY modifications and third-party hardware hacks is also giving smart glasses wearers unprecedented stealth by allowing them to disable the activation lights, either by bypassing the capture LEDs or by patching software to suppress system notifications.

Tech journalist Joanna Stern hosted a video showing the process in which a local hacker removed the LED light from her Ray-Ban Meta glasses for $100, allowing the wearables to secretly record without notice.

In a recent development, detecting active smart glasses in public or private spaces adds a new layer of security awareness, but it raises an obvious dilemma: What do you actually do with that information? Once a detector app alerts us that smart glasses are nearby, it seems our only choices are to either leave the space or ask the wearer to remove the glasses.

According to recent reports, uttara Ananthakrishnan, an associate professor of information systems at the University of Washington who studies the societal impacts of technology, says we’re still figuring out the social norms around wearables like smart glasses. It’s impossible to know whether the person filming will behave responsibly, and the question of consent gets even thornier if children might be captured on video or in photos.

Unlike with smartphones, where it’s easier to tell when someone is recording or taking photos, “smart glasses shift the burden of privacy entirely onto the person being photographed,” Ananthakrishnan said.

“Until we develop clear mechanisms to balance seamless innovation with consent, these devices will continue to turn everyday public spaces into zones of surveillance anxiety,” she mentioned.

That surveillance anxiety may prompt some hardware makers to release alternative versions of smart glasses that entirely avoid potential privacy violations.

Sources indicate that the Even G2 smart glasses don’t have a camera for recording photos or videos. They can pair with a separately sold R1 control ring that works as a fitness tracker.

For instance, Even Realities’ G2 smart glasses don’t include a front-facing camera at all. Instead, the Even G2 devices, released in late 2025, focus on providing the wearer with information and acting more like a personal assistant.

Sources indicate that “We made the decision from the beginning that smart glasses don’t need to have cameras on them in order to be useful,” Even Realities CEO Will Wang told CNET in an email. “We believe something worn on your face should respect not only the person wearing it, but everyone around them.”.

The G2 devices don’t record externally, a design choice Wang said gave the manufacturer a unique challenge. “Leaving the camera out also pushed us to think differently about what actually makes smart glasses useful day to day, rather than assuming more sensors automatically make a better product,” he said.

Wang said there’s room in the smart glasses market for different approaches to features and functionality, and that buyers may want to make trade-offs for devices they’ll wear on their faces. But Wang noted that the rise of smart glasses detectors indicates that social acceptance is an issue the industry needs to consider.

It has been revealed that over the last several months, smart glasses have been getting cheaper. And with more models and companies jumping into the fray, the demand for surveillance detectors is likely to grow — that is, unless Big Tech and wearable companies radically change their devices to make them invisible to detector apps.

Industry observers note that zuckoff’s Szydlowski said it’s possible a tech giant could shrink the kind of 5G technology to fit in smart glasses, making them less dependent on phones and Bluetooth, but that’s unlikely to happen anytime soon. If Meta or Snap deliberately updated their hardware to hide from detection apps and disable smart glasses’ digital footprint, it would further undercut any claim of privacy accountability.

Szydlowski remarked his hope is that, in time, Zuckoff won’t be needed at all. He pointed out that the ability to detect nearby Apple AirTag devices eventually became part of the operating systems on iOS and Android devices. If consumers pressure manufacturers and their governments to make smart glasses easier to detect, it would be “the perfect solution” to make his app obsolete, he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, phone-maker Nothing Technology is breaking away from its typical retro-inspired designs with a new pair of AI-powered earbuds, as reported earlier by Bloomberg. The organization confirmed via an X post that its Ear Note wireless earbuds will be available starting Dec. 8.

Sources indicate that the Ear Note earbuds are designed primarily to maximize the recording functionality. While other AI earbuds have already hit the market, the Ear Note is the first to record both phone calls and in-person conversations.

It has been revealed that the earbuds can capture and transcribe phone calls, while the charging case has its own microphone to record in-person conversations. To mitigate privacy concerns, the case only records with a physical button press — a tell that could reveal when audio is being captured around the Ear Note user.

Nothing shared that the Ear Note will work with multiple popular AI agents, but the full list of compatible software has not yet been released. The Ear Note works in tandem with an app that stores recordings from the earbuds and case, creating transcriptions and summaries similar to those created by the popular Otter AI app.

The Nothing brand has developed a cult following for combining lifestyle and fashion trends in its suite of smartphones, headphones, speakers and watches.

According to recent reports, the full product lineup is built with modern hardware, but mimics warm, nearly retrofuturist design sensibilities. The blocky Ear Note charging case continues this trend while taking the firm’s tech in a new direction.

In the lead-up to the Ear Note’s reveal, Nothing CEO Carl Pei described the earbuds in an X post as “a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product.”.

In a Bloomberg interview, Pei indicated that Nothing isn’t trying to create AI agents or software, but that the company has a “really interesting opportunity to be the hardware layer to AI.”.

It has been revealed that it’s currently unclear how much the Ear Note earbuds and case will cost when they’re released next month. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the company hasn’t settled on a price just yet. The most expensive earbuds currently available on the Nothing store cost $149.

Recent findings suggest that whether you’re covering your eyes, plugging your ears or slapping a timepiece on your wrist, there’s now an ever-present option to record the world around you. Multiple companies have created their own versions of smart glasses, earbuds and watches with augmented reality capabilities.

Now that AI is the flavor du jour, these existing features are being enhanced by new ways to scan and interact with the surrounding environment. That means a lot of visual and auditory data is being recorded by wearable devices, and very rarely with the consent of all parties involved.

The most immediate risk factors are associated with video recording – public distrust of smart glasses is so widespread that they’ve colloquially been coined “pervert glasses,” as folks fear they fundamentally break an unspoken social contract by obscuring public recording from other people.

But audio recording, enabled by Apple’s latest smartwatches, the Amazon Bee, Plaud earbuds and the newly introduced Ear Note, is also raising concerns, not least because many states require all-party consent before you can record conversations.

In a recent development, the Ear Note’s ability to record every bit of audio, from phone calls to in-person conversations, means it will be handling more sensitive information than other AI-powered earbuds. The company will need to face new challenges to ensure security measures are in place to prevent private chats from leaking.

Sources indicate that at the very least, it seems as though Nothing Technology is aware of these privacy risks. According to Bloomberg, the manufacturer created a data and security team to address concerns that cropped up during the Ear Note’s development. The company has also “obtained the same privacy certifications as competing recording products and worked with law firms to assess potential risks and safeguards.”.

Pei called wearables with recording functionality a sensitive space, and said the design team was “extra careful to not take any risks.” The Ear Note earbuds and case are largely controlled by user commands, including tactile button presses that begin the recording process.

“You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response remarked, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

Sources indicate that when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

Since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Upcoming York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

As both companies expand their digital platforms, determining which is the more attractive buy requires a look at their recent financial performance.

Axon Enterprise provides a comprehensive ecosystem of hardware and software designed for law enforcement and public safety professionals. Its product line includes Taser devices, body-worn cameras, and the Axon Evidence platform, which allows agencies to manage digital records securely. The company is actively expanding its presence among defense stocks and international markets across Europe and Asia. This growth was accompanied by a net income of approximately $258.5 million. The manufacturer continues to transition customers toward subscription-based software services, which typically offer higher visibility into future sales. This steady growth suggests strong demand for its integrated safety solutions among federal and local agencies.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.6x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholder equity, showing how much the tech giant relies on borrowed funds. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, is approximately 2.5x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was around $75.1 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 300% of operating cash flow, meaning reported cash generation is heavily inflated by this non-cash add-back.

Palantir Technologies develops platforms that integrate and analyze massive data sets to help organizations make better decisions.
