Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
  • How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
  • It has been revealed that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

It has been revealed that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

It has been revealed that title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

Industry observers note that first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

Industry observers note that “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

Industry observers note that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

Industry observers note that it can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

In a recent development, here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s upcoming £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

Industry observers note that city, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Industry observers note that throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

According to recent reports, had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal demonstrated was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

Gvardiol slides across to win an important challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

In a recent development, city soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

Recent findings suggest that in these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU.

City’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

The Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

It has been revealed that better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

According to recent reports, interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

According to recent reports, considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s massive names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the new season approaches.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

Arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

Odegaard tries a chipped pass into Havertz’s path in the penalty area but Gvardiol heads away. Moments earlier, Doku claimed he was fouled by White near the touchline but nothing doing.

Arsenal continue to flow forward, finding plenty of space in City’s half, but Tzolis’s cross deflects into the arms of Donnarumma.

There was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the new season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

Recent findings suggest that that’s certainly one way to start a fresh season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

Surely the fastest goal in the history of this fixture, or most fixtures for that matter.

Arsenal were camped in City’s half from kick off, and it was superb from Lewis-Skelly in midfield to let the ball run across his body and find the run of Calafiori with a reverse pass, and the left-back keeps his cool to roll the ball beyond Donnarumma.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

Arsenal get the game, and the 2026-27 domestic season, started.

Former Man City player Mike Summerbee, who fans used to hail with a Small Faces-inspired chant, is involved in the preliminaries.

Sources indicate that with no Timber, Saliba or Rice, this could be a more open game than some of the recent chess matches between these sides. The lower stakes should help with that. City have a favourable match up down their left with O’Reilly and Doku against Madueke and White. There is more ball retention in Arsenal’s team than at periods of last season, with Guimaraes, Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz in the middle.

Sources indicate that sincere commiserations to the Arsenal and Manchester City supporters who have attempted to travel by road to Cardiff today. We should have nothing but sympathy for those diehards who have tried to navigate the car parks of the M5 and the M4 and nothing but scorn for whoever is in charge of planning at Wembley. Who would have thought to check the football calendar before booking a concert for the week before the fresh season? A total nonsense. Let’s hope the game turns out to be better than the travel.

Always a talking point during the Six Nations, but there is no reason for it to close on a sunny afternoon on the banks of the River Taff. That will mean a slightly annoying shadow across the pitch, always a potential irritant in these August or May showpieces.

I mentioned already in the last days, no matter if we are in August or May, it is a final and when it is a final we need to win.

It has been revealed that [Players coming back from the World Cup] Many, many players, for us for them, we are in the exact same situation. It depends how we can manage the game, we will see.

According to recent reports, [What he expects from Anderson] Exactly the player he is. We are not asking him something more. He is a good player on and off the ball, always making an effort for his team-mates.

Recent findings suggest that I said in the press conference, we are going to decide the four captains when the window closes. At the moments, Ruben Dias and Erling are with us [no comment on Rodri’s future].

Sources indicate that good afternoon from Cardiff, where the sun is shining and the fans are enjoying the pubs outside the Principality Stadium. The teams are allowed nine substitutes today, which has really highlighted the bloated nature of Arsenal’s squad. There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

I had plenty of rest, some work as well, it was a break that I really enjoyed.

Very much [on if he was impressed with his signings]. Christos [Tzolis] came early which always helps with a new signing, and Bruno joined us last week after a long summer with him but he is in good condition.

It has been revealed that I think it is something very individual. [Declan] Rice played more than 65 games, he needed a complete rest and we need to build him. It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

It has been revealed that [On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

[On retaining the title] Still recognise the massive margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

According to recent reports, elliot Anderson makes his first City appearance, and he will be partnered by Mateo Kovacic in midfield with Nico O’Reilly drifting into those areas from midfield. Phil Foden, who did not go to the World Cup, starts ahead of Rayan Cherki and Doku, Haaland and Semenyo is City’s strongest front three. No Rodri, but Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland.

Subs: Rulli, Guéhi, Marmoush, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis.

The other interesting snippets are Arteta plumping for Madueke over Max Dowman on the right, Havertz over Gyokeres and Calafiori over Hincapie. Also worth noting that there is no place in the squad for Ethan Nwaneri nor Gabriel Martinelli who have been linked with moves. The same goes for Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson.

Arsenal starting XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Mikel names a strong starting XI 👊🤝Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/bckDyMazRo.

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

Recent findings suggest that in case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

Industry observers note that the pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Industry observers note that arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It has been revealed that it would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer plans remain up in the air for both camps.

City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

According to recent reports, although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the substantial games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

Sources indicate that need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected].

Recent findings suggest that BW LPG (BWLP +1.26%) reported its third quarter results, which management described as one of the strongest periods in organization history due to high shipping rates and substantial trading gains. Management stated that geopolitical factors and Panama Canal congestion continue to absorb fleet capacity by forcing longer trade routes around the Cape of Good Hope, which has pushed freight rates to record levels. The company reported that U.S. LPG exports reached all-time highs during the quarter, further increasing ton-mile demand. To capitalize on the current market, management is executing a fleet renewal strategy involving the sale of older vessels at record secondhand prices and the addition of eight Panamax VLGC newbuildings. The company indicated that a robust balance sheet and low leverage supported a dividend payout representing 100% of year-to-date shipping net profit after tax.

In a recent development, aline Anliker: Good morning, afternoon, evening, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. My name is Aline Anliker, and I'm the Head of Corporate Communications at BW LPG. On behalf of the management team, I'd like to extend a warm welcome to our shareholders, investors, analysts and valued stakeholders joining us for our quarterly earnings presentation. We appreciate you taking the time to be with us and for your continued interest and confidence in our organization. With me today are our CEO, Kristian Sorensen; CFO, Samantha Xu; as well as our Head of Investor Relations, Kaia Gaarud. In the next 30 minutes, Kristian and Samantha will walk you through the last quarter's performance, key market developments and our strategic priorities moving forward.

According to recent reports, following the presentation, we will open for a Q&A session. [Operator Instructions] Before we begin, I would like to draw your attention to the legal disclaimers shown on the current slide. Please also note that today's presentation is being recorded. And with that, it is my pleasure to hand over to our CEO, Kristian.

In a recent development, kristian Sørensen: Thanks, Aline, and hi, everyone. Thanks for joining us as we take you through our third quarter financial results with the company and market events from the quarter. Let's turn to Slide 4, please. The third quarter was again shaped by geopolitics and extensive market inefficiencies. Middle Eastern LPG exports remained well below normal levels, while U.S. LPG exports reached all-time highs and longer trade routes, combined with continued congestion in the Panama Canal absorbed substantial fleet capacity. As a result, the combination of our shipping and LPG trading portfolio made the third quarter one of the strongest quarters in our company's history. I will revisit the market developments in more detail in the market section.

In a recent development, moving on to the Q3 results. We reported a shipping TCE income of $84,100 per available day and $82,200 per calendar day after IFRS 15, FFA and other adjustments. This includes our fixed and index-linked time charter coverage of 51% of our available days at $54,300 per day. The result is below our guidance of $88,000 per day, primarily due to IFRS 15 and FFA adjustments. The Q3 profit after tax was $359 million with profit attributable to equity holders of USD 311 million. This is equivalent to an EPS of $2.05. This corresponds to an annualized return on equity of 66%.

Our trading business, BW Product Services generated a strong realized trading gain of $146 million during the quarter as well as an unrealized mark-to-market gain of $18 million. The gross profit was $163 million, and the profit after tax was $118 million. And as always, it's important to remember that it is the realized result which generates Product Services dividend capacity. Looking ahead for the fourth quarter, we are guiding on about $102,000 per day fixed for 92% of our available days. This includes our fixed time charter coverage of 43% at $44,200 per day and compares with our all-in cash breakeven reported of $24,900 per day.

In a recent development, please take a note that our TCE guidance excludes potential IFRS 15 and FFA impacts and the full breakdown of our quarterly time charter days and levels are to be found in the appendix in this presentation. The Board of Directors has declared a dividend of $1.30 per share, representing 92% payout of our shipping NPAT for the quarter and bringing the year-to-date dividend payout to 100% of our shipping NPAT. This is well ahead of the 75% set by our dividend policy given our net leverage ratio at 20% and translates into an annualized dividend yield of 24% based on our share price of $21.70 on Thursday, 19 November. Turning to other events.

Recent findings suggest that in September, we issued a 5-year $300 million senior unsecured convertible bond with a 2.25% coupon to partly finance our newbuilding program of 8 Panamax VLGCs. We also continued to capitalize on the strong secondhand market, and we unveiled the sale of the 2008-built BW Loyalty at a price in the low $80 million scheduled for delivery before the year-end. Two weeks ago, we also announced the sale of the 2015-built BW Mistral, which joined our fleet as part of the 2024 Avance Gas transaction.

This sale is expected to generate a net book gain of about $37 million and net cash proceeds of approximately $104 million with delivery by mid-January 2027 to the fresh buyers or to the new owners. It's worthwhile to mention that the vessel has generated a chartering revenue result of more than $58 million since she was delivered 2 years ago. Finally, the sale of the BW Birch and BW Levant, which we confirmed last quarter, the ships were delivered to the buyers in October and November, respectively. And with that, let's move on to the market overview. Next slide, please. Okay. Let's start with the map on the left.

It has been revealed that and structural inefficiencies continue to absorb fleet capacity, pushing freight rates to unprecedented levels. Under normal circumstances, the Middle East to the Far East and the U.S. Gulf to the Far East via the Panama Canal are the 2 key benchmark trades for our market. With the Strait of Hormuz still heavily constrained, Middle Eastern and LPG exports remain well below normal levels and Asian importers and India and Southeast Asia, in particular, are relying heavily on LPG from the U.S. instead. In absolute terms, however, China remained the largest destination for U.S. exports, while Japan remained the second largest as of end of Q3. As a result, the U.S. LPG exports are at all-time highs.

Industry observers note that with congestion and delays persisting in the Panama Canal during the third quarter, more of these cargoes sailed a much longer route around the Cape of Good Hope to India and the Far East, significantly increasing ton-mile demand. Moving into the fourth quarter, the canal has continued to operate at close to maximum capacity. And with transit availability uncertain, the dynamics have shifted towards more structural rerouting with vessels increasingly avoiding Panama altogether and planning voyages via the Cape of Good Hope. We're also seeing more ship-to-ship transfers in the Indian Ocean, which tie up additional vessels and further reduces the effective shipping capacity available for loading in the U.S. Gulf.

Industry observers note that the chart on the right shows how these factors have played out in freight rates this year. Following the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war, rates firmed significantly, reaching close to $200,000 per day in the spot markets. Back in May, when the U.S -Iran ceasefire MOU was signed, the market priced in a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. Far East arbitrage narrowed and the U.S. Gulf freight softened. As the sustained reopening failed to materialize, U.S. Far East rates recovered through the summer and an increased number of attacks on vessels in September have pushed rates even higher.

Lastly, secondhand asset prices are at record levels as the current elevated rate environment and the situation in the Middle East have pushed vessel values to all-time highs. And as you can see on this slide, we are harvesting value from record high secondhand prices while renewing our fleet at competitive newbuilding levels. The chart on the left highlights secondhand values translated into newbuilding equivalent value. And for the vintage built 2007 and 2008, the newbuilding equivalent has increased from around $150 million at the start of the year to about $280 million today. For 2015 and '16-built vessels, it has moved from around $135 million to about $200 million.

Sources indicate that and over the same period, newbuilding prices have remained relatively flat at around $116 million to $170 million for Korean yards. And in other words, the market is currently valuing our oldest vessels at more than twice the equivalent price of a newbuilding by adjusting for the vessel age. And we've taken advantage of this through disciplined countercyclical asset plays and this year, we sold the 2007-built BW Elm and BW Birch, the 2008-built BW Loyalty and the 2015-built BW Levant and the BW Mistral while ordering 8 Panamax VLGCs back in May. At the same time, with a more uncertain outlook moving into second half 2027, we continue to follow a balanced chartering strategy to protect the downside.

In a recent development, in Q3, 51% of our available days were covered by time charters with 42% on fixed rates averaging $46,300 per day. For Q4, our coverage is 53% with 43% fixed at $44,200 per day. And for 2027, we have already secured 42% fixed rate coverage, averaging $44,000 per day, which is up from 36% fixed rate coverage at the time of our last quarterly presentation. All of these levels are comfortably above our all-in cash breakeven of about $24,900 per day. And further information on our time charter portfolio can be found in the appendix at the end of the earnings presentation. Next slide, please. Turning to the fleet and the order book.

In a recent development, newbuilding contracting has been considerable with 108 VLGCs ordered so far in 2026, including our own 8 Panamax vessels. The total order book now stands at 177 VLGCs and yards are offering delivery slots in 2029 and well into 2030. As the delivery schedule on the left reveals, 41 VLGCs have been delivered so far this year. We expect an elevated pace of deliveries in the coming years, peaking at around 20 vessels in the fourth quarter of 2029. The global fleet now stands at 451 VLGCs on the water, which is up from 437 as per last reported quarter. At the same time, the fleet continues to age.

And today, 8% of the fleet is 25 years or older and another 5% is between 20 and 25 years of age. By the end of 2030, 127 VLGCs will be 20 years or older compared to 68 vessels at the end of this year. As we said before, the LPG exports will continue to grow and how this order book is absorbed will depend on the inefficiencies in the market, including trade patterns, Panama Canal transits and sailing distances as well as the phaseout of older tonnage. Next slide, please. Finally, let's take a look at the LPG export outlook. And our forecast assumes a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz in 2027.

Sources indicate that north American VLGC exports are expected to grow by 17% this year to around 70 million tonnes, cushioning the Middle East shortfall with further growth to around 74 million tonnes in 2028. Middle Eastern VLGC exports are expected to fall to around 18 million tonnes this year, which is 27 million tonnes short of the pre-war forecast. Assuming a reopening, we expect a gradual recovery supported by latest projects with a shortfall versus the pre-war forecast narrowing to 20 million tonnes in 2027 and 14 million tonnes in 2028. This is because, as we have mentioned before, it will take time to repair production and export infrastructure and recovery time remains uncertain.

Looking at the middle chart, this graph is taken from Enterprise Products Partners' earnings presentation in October and shows the U.S. NGL production forecasted to grow about 34% from 2025 to 2030, roughly 2.4x the growth rate of crude oil. While crude oil production growth is expected to moderate, rising gas-to-oil ratios and richer gas streams continue to support NGL production growth. And turning to export capacity, close to 30 million tonnes of additional North American LPG export capacity is expected to come online from second half 2026 to second half of 2028. And these expansions will be important in allowing continued growth in U.S. NGL production to translate into higher LPG exports and ultimately increased demand for VLGC shipping.

Industry observers note that and to sum up, geopolitics and trade patterns continue to create inefficiencies that absorb shipping capacity, while the medium-term outlook is underpinned by growing North American exports and a gradual recovery of Middle Eastern volumes. The timing of a Hormuz reopening and general Panama Canal congestion remain key wildcards, while the growing pace of newbuilding deliveries increases the uncertainty as we move into 2027. And that concludes our market segment. I guess it's over to you, Samantha.

Samantha Xu: Thank you, Kristian. Hello, everyone. Let's dive into what was an incredible quarter. Our shipping business delivered TCE income of $84,100 per available day or $82,200 per calendar day. This includes negative IFRS 15 and FFA adjustments of USD 14.9 million and USD 20.2 million, respectively. Before these accounting effects, which our guidance excluded, our underlying performance was ahead of guidance. The underlying spot performance was very strong. $115,300 per available day, including waiting time and FFA and USD 123,000 per day, excluding both. That highlights the earning quality of our platform in a volatile market. Fleet utilization was 97%, reflecting a very strong execution.

It has been revealed that among the uncertainties, we remain prudent, focusing on downside protection through our time charter portfolio and active FFA risk management. In Q3, 51% of our available days were covered by time charter, out of which 42% were fixed rate time charters. Looking ahead for Q4 2026, we have fixed 92% of the available fleet days at an average rate of about USD 102,000 per day. This also includes index-linked time charter contracts, so the final rate may still move with the spot market. Looking at 2027, we have secured 42% of our portfolio through fixed rate time charter at USD 44,000 per day.

This fixed rate time charter portfolio is expected to generate approximately USD 229 million of revenue in 2027, and that gives us a solid earning visibility while keeping our exposure to a strong spot market. Coming to Product Services performance. Product Services delivered an exceptional realized trading gain of USD 146 million in Q3, a great achievement in a turbulent market. The reported result also includes a net realized (sic) [ unrealized ] mark-to-market gain of USD 80 million (sic) [ USD 18 million ], representing USD 82 million increase on cargo positions, partly offset by USD 65 million decrease on paper positions. Gross profit was USD 163 million.

After G&A and tax, profit after tax was USD 118 million with the net asset value arrived at USD 216 million at quarter end. The realized result demonstrates the value of our integrated cargo, paper and shipping platform. The unrealized mark-to-market movements simply reflects valuations at a balance sheet date and can swing in volatile markets until positions are realized. As such, trading gains and losses are realized across different periods and cannot be extrapolated from past performance. It's also worth noting that the reported net asset value excludes the unrealized physical shipping position of USD 170 million at the balance sheet date based on the internal valuation.

In Q3, our average VaR value at risk was USD 18 million, reflecting continued market volatility and the added cargo from our term contracts. We expect the VaR to stay elevated as the market remains volatile and our term contract book builds from late 2026 into 2027. Turning to our financial highlights. We reported net profit after tax of USD 359 million. Profit attributable to equity holder was $311 million or $2.05 per share, representing an annualized earning yield of 33% based on the period-end share price. This includes a one-off gain from the sale of a BW Elm. We reported a net leverage ratio of 20% in Q3, down from the 23.5% at the end of Q2 '26.

The Board declared a dividend of $1.30 per share. That is 92% of shipping NPAT for the quarter and brings the year-to-date payout to 100% of shipping NPAT. Measured against the total profit to equity holders, it is a 63% payout for the quarter. Product Services profit is evaluated for distribution only after the financial year-end. Our dividend policy is 75% payout ratio when leverage ratio is at or above 20%. At 100% of year-to-date shipping NPAT, we are well ahead of that. This reflects our strong performance, solid liquidity position and our confidence in the near-term market.

It has been revealed that we continue to take a forward-leaning approach to return earnings to shareholders in this strong market, while strengthening our balance sheet for fleet renewal and growth. At period end, the shareholders' equity was $2.3 billion. Annualized return on equity was 66% and return on capital employed 53%. Q3 OpEx was $8,800 per day. For 2026, we expect operating cash breakeven of about $18,300 per day for the owned fleet and $21,700 per day for the total fleet, including chartering vessels. All-in cash breakeven, including maintenance and dry dock CapEx is about $24,900 per day. In September, we issued USD 300 million of 5-year senior unsecured convertible bond with a 2.25% coupon and a 40% conversion premium.

According to recent reports, the proceeds fund predelivery cost of our newbuilding and further strengthens our liquidity. As a result, we maintained a strong liquidity of USD 859 million at the quarter end, consisting of USD 317 million in cash and -- sorry, USD 542 million of undrawn revolving credit facilities. By Dana George – Nov 24, 2026 at 3:15PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF ›.

Unlike a bull or bear market, there's not always a clear sign that a recession has arrived. There may be subtle signs -- like slowed GDP growth or high unemployment -- but there's no single factor that sets off recession alarm bells.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, a recession may be officially declared many months after it's already begun, or even after it's ended. And frankly, that bothers me.

Sources indicate that as someone who prefers to plan ahead, I find it maddening that I can't always spot a recession before it hits my investments. Fortunately, I'm in the middle of rebalancing my portfolio, and as part of that process, I've been looking for an ETF that can serve as a hedge against the next recession -- whenever that may be.

I do believe I've found one that will work.

Sources indicate that I have no way of knowing if a recession will hit in 2027, or how markets will respond if one does. However, I have decided that the one ETF to help steady my portfolio through the next economic storm should be the Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF (BND +0.00%).

Buying BND helps balance out some of the stocks in my portfolio by providing broad exposure to investment-grade U.S. bonds. I know it's not recession-proof or a replacement for cash, but it may help soften the ups and downs -- which matters to someone like me who worries about market swings.

It has been revealed that I've come to view bond funds as a risk reduction strategy. In a recession, investors tend to be more cautious about tech giant earnings and stock prices, and many will sell, hoping to avoid losses. Rather than tying investors' money to a single company or industry, BND spreads the risk across many issuers.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

Bonds don't always move in the same direction as stocks. If a recession brings lower interest rates, existing bonds with higher yields may become more valuable. That's not a sure thing, but it's one reason I'm drawn to BND.

There's certainly more to protecting a portfolio than balancing or diversifying. It's also important to keep investment costs low and match risk to when I'll need the money.

But in times like these, when I'm not sure when the next recession will occur, I feel good about a fund that can provide steady dividends now and help protect my portfolio when the market becomes volatile.

I Rate Buy Now, Pay Later Apps; Here’s My Holiday Advice

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

It’s a big list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

Industry observers note that I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) blueprint to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL users expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

In a recent development, brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, says many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

“They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison says. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”.

Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

While Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how key it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison says BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

“With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he says.

Not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

There are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

Recent findings suggest that long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

In a recent development, pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

In a recent development, harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL organization doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

In a recent development, because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

It has been revealed that according to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL consumers had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison notes.

In a recent development, “If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he says. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”.

Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

Still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison states, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

“Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he states. “There's a massive difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”.

Despite ongoing geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and evolving global trade policies, the company continues to execute its massive newbuilding program and strategic investments in related shipping sectors.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Danaos Corporation conference call to discuss the financial results for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026. As a reminder, today's call is being recorded. Please also note that where we feel appropriate, we will continue to refer to non-GAAP financial measures such as EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income, time charter equivalent revenues and time charter equivalent dollars per day to evaluate our business. Reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures to GAAP financial measures are included in our earnings release and accompanying materials. With that, let me now turn the call over to Dr. John Coustas, who will provide the broad overview of the quarter. John?

John Coustas: Thank you, Evangelos. Good morning, and thank you all for joining today's call to discuss results for the third quarter of 2026. The geopolitical picture was largely unchanged during the quarter with no visible end to the conflict. The one significant development is that transits through the Bab al-Mandab Strait have become more regular. Liners are gradually moving tonnage back through the Suez Canal, and say for new developments, Red Sea traffic could be restored in the first quarter of 2027. Despite this shift, the container market continued to strengthen, and the liner companies reported strong third quarter results. Open tonnage remains scarce, and the charter market has strengthened with it.

We used those conditions to add approximately $611 million to our contracted revenue backlog, which now stands at $5 billion, with our container fleet 100% contracted for 2026, 94% for 2027, 84% for 2028, 71% for 2029 and 53% for 2030 at healthy rates. The Capesize market also strengthened with charter rates at multiyear highs, and our dry bulk segment contributed $22.4 million of adjusted EBITDA for the quarter against $9.1 million a year ago. We decided to defer the carve-out and sale of a minority stake in the segment in the Norwegian market for now so that any transaction is executed at the time and on terms that optimize value for our shareholders.

In a recent development, the Board declared a special dividend of $5 per share and raised the quarterly dividend to $1 per share, in line with our policy of rewarding shareholders. In October, we marked 20 years since our listing on the Fresh York Stock Exchange, and Moody's upgraded our senior unsecured notes to Ba1 and changed the outlook of our Ba1 corporate family rating to positive, which confirms our solid performance and financial strength. With that, I'll hand the call over back to Evangelos, who will take you through the financials for the quarter.

Evangelos Chatzis: Thank you, John, and good morning again to everyone. I will review the results for the quarter, and we will then open the call to Q&A. Adjusted net income for the third quarter was $152.1 million or $8.32 per share compared with $124.1 million or $6.75 per share in the third quarter of 2025. That is an increase of $28 million or approximately 23% on a per share basis.

According to recent reports, this improvement is the combined result of a $23.6 million increase in operating revenues a $4.6 million reduction in net finance expenses and a $5.3 million increase in dividend income by our Star Bulk holding, partially offset by a $5.2 million increase in total operating expenses and $0.3 million increase in loss of equity investments. Let me start with revenues. Container vessel revenue increased by $8.7 million to $247.8 million total. Our newbuilding deliveries contributed an incremental $8.2 million, reflecting one 6,000 TEU vessel delivery in the fourth quarter of 2025 that commenced a 7-year charter and three 8,250 TEU vessels that joined the fleet in the current quarter, each commencing a 5-year charter.

Industry observers note that lower off-hire added a further $4.3 million with container fleet utilization improving to 99.6% this quarter from 98.1% a year ago and higher charter rates contributed $0.3 million. Offsetting these was a $4.1 million reduction in noncash revenue recognition under U.S. GAAP. Dry bulk revenue increased by $14.9 million or 69% to $36.5 million in the current quarter from $21.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. The principal driver, of course, was the strength of the Capesize market, and our dry bulk time charter equivalent rate rose to $32,690 per day from $19,910 per day in the comparable quarter, while we also operated additional Cape vessel that joined our fleet during the second quarter of this year.

In a recent development, as a result, the dry bulk segment adjusted EBITDA increased to $22.4 million compared to $9.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, and the net income rose to $15.8 million from $3.4 million a year ago. Turning now to operating costs. Vessel operating expenses came in at $53.3 million, up only $1 million from the $52.3 million number posted in Q3 of 2025, notwithstanding the increase in the average number of vessels in our fleet. Our daily operating costs declined to $6,790 per day from $6,927 per day a year ago. Our operating costs remain among the most competitive in the industry.

G&A expenses increased by $1.5 million to $14.1 million from $12.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and the increase relates mainly to higher management fees while corporate G&A was -- came in marginally lower this quarter. On the finance cost side, interest expense, excluding amortization of finance fees and debt discount, increased by $1.4 million to $9.2 million in the current quarter, up from $7.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. And there are 2 components to that. Average indebtedness increased by approximately $0.5 billion to $1.29 billion this quarter as we drew on our committed financing for our newbuilding deliveries. And that added $5 million in interest expense.

Industry observers note that this effect was meaningfully mitigated by a reduction in our average cost of debt service of approximately 1.3%, reflecting lower SOFR rates and the lower coupon following the refinancing of our bond. Working in the other direction, capitalized interest on vessels under construction rose to $9.6 million from $6 million as our newbuilding program advanced, reducing interest expense by $3.6 million. At the same time, interest income increased by $6 million to $9.8 million this quarter from $3.8 million a year ago, obviously driven by higher average cash balances.

Recent findings suggest that we also received $5.6 million in dividends from our Star Bulk shareholding this quarter compared to $3.8 million a year ago -- sorry, compared to $0.3 million in the third quarter of last year. Adjusted EBITDA increased by 14.2% or $25.7 million to $207.3 million compared to $181.6 million in the third quarter of 2025 for the reasons that have already been outlined on this call. We would encourage you to review our updated investor presentation and the subsequent events disclosures, both of which are available on our website. Turning to some of the highlights. Since the date of our last earnings release, we have added approximately $611 million to our contracted revenue backlog.

As a result, our backlog now stands at a record level of $5 billion with a 4.5-year average remaining charter duration, while contract coverage has already been outlined by John earlier. Within our investor presentation, you will find analytical disclosure on our charter contracts. On the fleet side, in September, we added two 9,000 TEU container ships to our order book for delivery in the first quarter of 2029. Our order book now comprises of 28 container ships with an aggregate capacity of approximately 178,000 TEU and 4 Newcastlemax dry bulk vessels.

According to recent reports, on a fully delivered basis, our fleet will consist of 106 container ships of approximately 680,000 TEU and 15 dry bulk vessels, combination of Capes and Newcastlemaxes with a capacity of approximately 2.8 million deadweight. On the financing side, in August, we entered into an additional $200 million Japanese Operating Lease financing transactions with a tenor of 8 years for 2 of our newbuildings that were delivered to us in September of this year. Both transactions have now been consummated. In September, given our strong liquidity position and our committed newbuilding financing, we canceled our revolving credit facility, which was undrawn and was scheduled to mature in December of 2027.

Also in October, Moody's upgraded our senior unsecured notes to Ba1 and moved the outlook on our Ba1 corporate family rating to positive. As of September 30, net debt came in at $327.9 million, equivalent to 0.43x over last 12 months EBITDA. And out of our current fleet of 89 vessels, 78 are unencumbered and debt-free. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two upcoming credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

In a recent development, the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

According to recent reports, they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

In a recent development, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for upcoming applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

It has been revealed that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

It has been revealed that to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

According to recent reports, wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Industry observers note that travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in New York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Industry observers note that bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

It has been revealed that however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

The earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

It has been revealed that plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

Those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

In a recent development, one of the most interesting perks of the upcoming cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

In a recent development, there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card.

Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

The revenue trend is the most obvious metric for investors to examine when considering a stock. The first thing to check for when examining a tech giant's revenue trend is seasonality: some times of the year have stronger buying patterns than others. There usually is some seasonality for every business.

Even in pharmaceuticals, there is seasonality, with the end of the calendar year seeing higher prescription activity as consumers and doctors front-load prescriptions after insurance deductibles have been met, before they reset with the latest year.

Michael Creedon: Yes. Thanks, Rupesh. Well, look, I'll build on some of my comments that I made in the earlier question against 2027. But look, I'll start by saying we've seen this movie before. Dollar Tree has navigated these kind of headwinds on freight and other costs for 40 years. And for most of that time, we were a single price point retailer. And for a long time, we bought and managed the margin. So I just want people to understand that as I give you these comments on freight because freight is an area of pressure, particularly as we cycle last year's favorable freight environment. And I just break it into 2 pieces.

According to recent reports, you've got direct imports and you've got domestic transportation. On imports, we've got good visibility into the ocean freight costs. And I'd say the majority of our volume is under 1-year contracts with a smaller amount on multiyear contracts. And so that -- those 1 years are going to renew, of course, every year. The spot rates, the spot loads are sort of mid-single digits. So they're a relatively small part of our portfolio. And that import group, just to help you dimensionalize this, is about 1/3 overall of our freight, our overall transportation costs.

Recent findings suggest that we've taken benefit this year from favorable ocean rates generally as against history and lower spot usage, but we've seen higher fuel costs offsetting that, and those come in surcharges. And I said last quarter, those surcharges, of course, will move up and down with the price of fuel. So I think over the long haul, that's probably a positive. On the domestic side, we contract those rates by lane with carriers. And the challenge right now is that there's a very tight driver market. And when those carriers don't have enough drivers, we have to rely more on the higher cost surge drivers.

Recent findings suggest that so domestically, we're dealing with higher fuel costs and a tight driver market and on imports, that pressure is coming from fuel. With respect to your sort of rule of thumb, the best way I could describe that is that on the 2/3, which is the domestic transportation, about $1 in diesel price is worth somewhere around $40 million of annual cost to us. So meaningful but manageable. On the direct -- on the import side, it's much more complicated because of shifting countries, contract rates, surcharges and therefore, I'm hesitant to sort of give you a rule of thumb on that. But the good news is, look, we've got a well-established playbook on this.

And I just want to remind everybody on this call the sort of 5 levers that we use in managing these kinds of costs. Supplier. We've got supplier renegotiation to push back on the cost, reengineering products and pack sizes to accommodate the price point, discontinuing items that cannot meet the margin targets. We have seen shift in countries of origin to accommodate lowest cost product. And finally, the last point for us is optimizing pricing. And we view that as a last step. So hopefully, that gives you a full picture of freight and how we manage it.

What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
  • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
  • An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any issues are documented.

A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

Service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

According to recent reports, detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

It has been revealed that reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

It has been revealed that however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

It has been revealed that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

Recent findings suggest that some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

In a recent development, reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Reddit users are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several users suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
  • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
  • Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

One key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

In a recent development, another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

Just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a latest region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit key sites when off the ship.

If there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy shows, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Recent findings suggest that many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

In a recent development, if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

Recent findings suggest that keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

It has been revealed that this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Upcoming York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

Departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and New England before reaching the Big Apple.

Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching Upcoming York.
