📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

Recent findings suggest that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

In a recent development, as it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

Industry observers note that “They know how to do it,” Arteta stated of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”.

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard mentioned. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”.

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard remarked Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt.

It has been revealed that before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Another day, another substantial swing.
  • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Industry observers note that the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

It has been revealed that my point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Sources indicate that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to newly introduced inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

In a recent development, mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

In a recent development, strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI indicated wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

Sources indicate that predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

It has been revealed that markets are right now anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

But back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

» Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

In a recent development, » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a fresh home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

It has been revealed that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#85131. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1042 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1042 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Recent findings suggest that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

It has been revealed that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," remarked Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he mentioned.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone noted.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That noted, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

Sources indicate that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, remarked Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

"We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

Recent findings suggest that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, mentioned Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

Recent findings suggest that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

It has been revealed that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she mentioned.

Industry observers note that "It is isolated," she remarked. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

Recent findings suggest that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

Recent findings suggest that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin noted. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It's also key to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo noted.

Industry observers note that "That's when spreads really widen out," he remarked. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

#85127. B2B Companies Should Stop Letting B2C Set Their Digital Commerce Roadmap

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (834 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

B2B Companies Should Stop Letting B2C Set Their Digital Commerce Roadmap

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (834 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jary Carter is CEO and Co-Founder of Oro Inc., the manufacturer behind OroCommerce, a B2B eCommerce platform for manufacturers and distributors.
  • ​For years, B2B companies have taken their cues on digital progress from consumer commerce.
  • As the CEO of an e-commerce platform who works closely with B2B partners, I can tell you that never happened.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jary Carter is CEO and Co-Founder of Oro Inc., the manufacturer behind OroCommerce, a B2B eCommerce platform for manufacturers and distributors.

​For years, B2B companies have taken their cues on digital progress from consumer commerce. Amazon was treated as the model that B2B would eventually have to follow, with every buying experience starting to look more like Amazon.

As the CEO of an e-commerce platform who works closely with B2B partners, I can tell you that never happened. Amazon became another channel, not the blueprint for B2B commerce.​.

Recent findings suggest that now agentic purchasing is getting similar treatment. B2B companies have seen this pattern before: A consumer trend gets treated as the future of commerce before anyone asks how well it fits B2B.

So what happens when that thinking starts setting the digital commerce roadmap?

Sources indicate that consumer commerce tends to treat less human involvement as progress. Search, buy, check out, done.​.

B2B buyers want plenty of independence, too. But taking the seller out of the experience can take valuable context out with them. ​.

It has been revealed that for many B2B companies, the seller’s knowledge of the customer is part of the competitive advantage. Digital commerce should build on that advantage, not erase it.​.

Industry observers note that one specialty distributor we work with learned this the hard way. Its first e-commerce launch struggled so badly that leadership questioned whether digital selling made sense for the business at all. The team later described the experience as “anonymous e-commerce” because it separated buyers from their account context and the people who knew them.​.

Industry observers note that on its second attempt, the company brought account management straight into the digital experience. Customers could see their dedicated rep inside the portal, while sales and service staff used impersonation to handle onboarding, guide first orders and troubleshoot on the fly.​.

Buyers still get the independence they wanted. The difference is that going digital no longer cuts them off from the people who know their account.​.

It has been revealed that A retail-style roadmap can make the seller look like friction to remove. In B2B, digital commerce should do the opposite: Give the buyer-seller relationship a place to continue online.

The same problem shows up in how commerce teams define flexibility. The conversation often stays at the experience layer: change the storefront faster, launch a upcoming journey, test a different way to buy.​.

In a recent development, useful. But B2B companies usually discover the limits of their technology somewhere else.​.

Sources indicate that can you bring an acquired business onto the same setup when it has a different ERP? Add a region with its own catalog and pricing rules? Change an approval process or introduce a latest sales model without rebuilding half the system?​.

Recent findings suggest that A tech giant can have a highly flexible front end and still struggle with changes like these. Being able to redesign the buying experience swiftly doesn’t mean the commerce setup can adapt quickly to the business behind it.​​.

For B2B, flexibility is tested when the business changes, not when the homepage does. The roadmap has to account for that.

Recent findings suggest that AI is the newest version of the same pattern. Retail attention has centered on shopping agents, conversational discovery and AI that can research or complete a purchase.

Those ideas may have a place in B2B, too. They just aren’t automatically the best place to start.​.

In B2B, AI can play a different role: help sellers know their buyers better, surface customer and deal information faster and take repetitive work out of the sales process.​.

In a recent development, while my company’s platform offers AI features, which certainly shapes my view on this topic, the shift I’m pointing to is about identifying where AI makes the most sense in B2B rather than which tools to adopt. ​.

Recent findings suggest that more than 75% of B2B orders still arrive through email, PDFs, spreadsheets, voicemail or handwritten notes, according to Distribution Strategy Group. Their research found that AI-based order processing can deliver productivity gains of 20% to 30%. Gartner also found that AI is already saving sellers an average of 4.8 hours per week.​.

Some of the highest-value AI in B2B may sit far from the storefront. That is why copying the retail roadmap can send investment toward the most visible use cases instead of the most valuable ones.

Watch what B2C does with search, usability and convenience. But it should not decide what progress looks like for your B2B business. ​.

In a recent development, the next priority should come from the processes your company needs to improve, the relationships it needs to strengthen and the markets it plans to enter. Use retail for inspiration. But don’t adopt its story. B2B has a more interesting one to tell. ​.

Normally, the first thing to note when examining a manufacturer's revenue trend is seasonality: some times of the year have stronger buying patterns than others. For most stocks, compare revenue year over year, by quarter. In normal times, seasonality holds true for consumer stocks like these as well.

Booking Holdings gets exceptional volume for summer months in the Northern Hemisphere, which translates into seasonally high revenue being registered in the third quarter.

Ultimately, such a decision comes down to risk tolerance: the more steady revenue a business has, the less volatile its stock price will be, but the higher-sales, more volatile tech giant will probably see greater rewards from the market over time.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

Why Connectivity Needs To Become Programmable

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that mobile networks were designed with a person at the end of every connection.
  • Industry observers note that that design fits a shrinking share of the people and things now using networks.
  • After years of building connectivity for travelers and distributed teams, I see these as one problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dmitri Verbovski, Yesim Founder.

Industry observers note that mobile networks were designed with a person at the end of every connection. A contract carries a name, and a initiative is sized for one phone. When something breaks, someone calls support or walks into a store.

Industry observers note that that design fits a shrinking share of the people and things now using networks. Delivery robots, connected cars, smart meters and medical wearables are among the fastest-growing owners, and none of them has a name on a contract. At the same time, AI assistants handle more everyday tasks for people, but connectivity is still largely out of their reach.

After years of building connectivity for travelers and distributed teams, I see these as one problem. Whether the user is a person or a device, the connection should be set up and managed through software. In other words, connectivity has to become programmable.

Recent findings suggest that but machines don’t sign contracts, so someone has to own the relationship on their behalf. They also move: A sensor shipped from a factory in Poland may spend its working life in Brazil. Their usage looks nothing like a person’s. A smart meter sends a few kilobytes a day for 10 years, while a robotaxi can move gigabytes in an afternoon, and a consumer-style plan suits neither.

People run into the same friction, though it’s less visible. In our support conversations, the hardest questions are usually about status rather than speed: Is my plan active? Why did data stop at the border? Which line am I paying for? A well-designed system should answer those without requiring a support ticket.

Ericsson counted around 4.5 billion cellular IoT connections at the end of 2025 and expects that number to approach 8 billion by 2031. Its June 2026 Mobility Report also notes that uplink traffic is growing faster than downlink for most operators, and that additional AI traffic could push uplink to three times its 2025 level by 2031.

Software is also starting to act for people. Gartner predicted that 40% of enterprise applications would include task-specific AI agents by 2026, up from less than 5% in 2025. If an assistant can book your hotel, people will reasonably expect it to get them online at the destination as well. Today, that step usually leads to a QR code or a carrier portal designed for manual clicks.

Put these trends together, and more connectivity decisions will be made by software acting on someone’s behalf.

A SIM in every device connects the device, but it doesn’t make the connection manageable. Programmable connectivity means the connection itself can be requested, switched, limited and retired through APIs, much as cloud platforms let teams manage servers. I think that requires four capabilities.

According to recent reports, • Delegated Identity: Every connection should be traceable to an accountable owner such as a tech giant or a fleet operator, even when software manages it. Otherwise, fraud and misuse are very hard to attribute.

• Programmatic Provisioning: Devices without screens can’t scan QR codes. The GSMA’s SGP.32 specification already allows eSIM profiles on IoT devices to be downloaded, switched and retired remotely. The next step is exposing that capability through APIs, so a fleet platform, an app or an AI assistant can arrange connectivity on demand.

It has been revealed that • Policy And Spend Controls: Software should manage connectivity within set limits: which networks, which regions, how much data and what maximum cost. Finance teams already set budgets for cloud usage, and connectivity should work the same way.

In a recent development, • Life Cycle Portability: A connected car or medical device may outlive three generations of network technology and several carrier contracts. Its connectivity has to move with it, across borders and providers, without anyone opening the casing.

Our enterprise customers rarely struggle with the first activation. Problems tend to come months later, when an employee relocates or a device changes hands. Those are the moments where programmable connectivity saves the most time.

Recent findings suggest that A fair objection is that operators will build this themselves, and some already are. Network slicing reserves guaranteed performance for specific use cases, and Ericsson counted 84 commercial offerings built on it in June 2026, up from 65 seven months earlier.

It has been revealed that I see the roles as complementary. An operator runs its own network. A platform layer works across networks: countries, operators, device types and budgets. A car built in Germany, sold in Brazil and driven across borders needs both.

Recent findings suggest that I learned this from travel. Travelers plan around destinations, such as Lisbon on Monday and Madrid on Thursday, rather than around operators. The platform’s job is to match that plan with the right network at the right price, without asking anyone to understand roaming agreements. eSIM is what makes this workable: Because the SIM profile is software, a a network identity can be switched or retired remotely, whether on a phone or on a sensor bolted to a shipping container.

According to recent reports, imagine booking a trip through an assistant that, with your permission, also arranges a local data strategy within a budget you’ve set. You land, turn off airplane mode and you’re online.

For the person at the center, programmable connectivity should mean fewer decisions. People don’t want to have to compare roaming rates, scan QR codes or follow up on support tickets. Connectivity works best when people don’t have to think about it, and making it programmable is a practical way to get there.​.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Sources indicate that A lot has changed for Nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) in a very short period of time, and this will ultimately have a substantial impact on where the semiconductor stock trades by the end of 2027. Given the stock's strong performance over the years, it tends to be widely held by retail investors. With a lot on the line, let's see where the stock could be headed over the next year.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest change for Nvidia comes at the top. In a shocking turn of events, co-founder Jensen Huang, who had been the only CEO in the company's history, resigned earlier this month only to be welcomed back by the board less than two weeks later. Huang stepped down after he admitted marital infidelity as reports of multiple affairs bubbled to the surface. Investors focused on his relationship with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation), who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Sources indicate that singapore-based Megaspeed has been a significant Nvidia customer, buying nearly $5 billion worth of its chips over the past few years. However, there are now allegations that many of these chips were illegally being directed to China.

The return of Jensen Huang as CEO for Nvidia is huge. Huang was a visionary who seemingly knew where the market was headed before anyone else. There are multiple examples of the company taking action based on his foresight, including:.

These have all helped the company transform from a simple chipmaker into a complete AI infrastructure company that has been getting an increasingly larger percentage of spending per gigawatt of compute capacity.

However, there is still a question of what happens with China. The U.S. has further cracked down on export controls of AI chips. The risk is that there is a lot more indirect Nvidia revenue coming from China, which could disappear.

In a recent development, the Huang situation is not the only news Nvidia has endured this month, though. The midterm elections saw a sweeping victory for Democrats and candidates that ran on anti-data-center campaigns. These candidates have widely called for a data center build-out moratorium, and it is expected that the regulatory environment for building upcoming data centers will get a lot tougher in the coming years. Neoclouds are expected to face the brunt of this, which could be bad news for Nvidia, which saw about 44% of its data center revenue last quarter coming from neoclouds and businesses.

On top of this, Anthropic (ANT -6.54%) revealed that its Claude Mythos model was able to switch models running on Nvidia's GPUs to run on Advanced Micro Devices' (AMD -8.86%) GPUs with little human intervention in just a few days. This process used to take six to 12 months and a dozen engineers. This could be a serious blow to Nvidia's CUDA moat and eventually lead to lower prices and serious gross margin compression.

That noted, Nvidia is still well positioned in the medium term, as it has significant supply chain advantages. It has locked up a substantial amount of the supply-constrained high bandwidth memory (HBM) required by AI chips, as well as capacity at foundries. In addition, with its Vera Rubin platform, it is now getting $40 billion per gigawatt of compute capacity compared to the $25 billion per gigawatt it is capturing with Grace Blackwell, which is a significant revenue lift. This will help support the 75% growth the firm projected for fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) and beyond.

The issues Nvidia faces are likely to keep a cap on its forward P/E multiple, but it should still see solid growth in the medium term. I think it should be able to maintain a forward multiple of at least 12, which would value the stock at around $261 at the end of 2027 based on the fiscal 2029 analyst consensus of $21.75. As such, a $10,000 investment today — getting you 61 shares as I write this — would be worth over $15,900. That’s my prediction.

There is some decent upside to the AI stock from its current beaten-down levels, despite potential risks.

​Building A Data Foundation That Makes Enterprise AI Work

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Niraj Nagrani is Chief Data and AI Officer at Altimetrik.
  • After more than 30 years as an enterprise leader, I’ve been through many transformation journeys, from building hyperscale systems and training data for machine learning to migrating from legacy architectures to modern data platforms.
  • The problem is not with foundation models, which have improved exponentially over the past few years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Niraj Nagrani is Chief Data and AI Officer at Altimetrik.

After more than 30 years as an enterprise leader, I’ve been through many transformation journeys, from building hyperscale systems and training data for machine learning to migrating from legacy architectures to modern data platforms. Today, I see many organizations struggle to move from a successful AI pilot to a reliable production system​.

The problem is not with foundation models, which have improved exponentially over the past few years. In my experience, the problem almost always comes back to the underlying data architecture.

According to recent reports, many organizations are still working with data that isn’t ready for AI. Data quality and lineage may be governed inconsistently or not governed at all. And governance is often bolted on at the end rather than built in from the start.

In a recent development, I’ve worked with companies running over 100 siloed systems. When information is scattered that widely, it can be almost impossible to establish a consistent view of the business. Unstructured data like contracts, emails and support tickets can disappear into blind spots because they don’t fit neatly into traditional data structures. Another problem is the lack of a shared definition of business entities like revenue, customers or other important measures across systems. ​.

Industry observers note that earlier machine learning learned patterns from a curated, labeled dataset to do one narrow task. Agents reason and act in real time across systems. At the moment of action, an agent has to know what a “customer” means, which policy applies, whether the data is current and what it is allowed to see. Without that context, you get a confident wrong action. Earlier machine learning needed clean training data; agents need living context.

Industry observers note that the key first step of data modernization is what I call “business rule archaeology.” Over time, organizations accumulate business logic in stored procedures, SQL queries and their dependencies. Some of that logic is documented, but a lot of it isn’t, which makes it difficult to understand how the existing business processes actually work. Companies often underestimate the effort required to untangle these dependencies.​.

In a recent development, before planning for​ modernization, understand how the business uses its data and how its processes operate. From there, organizations can build an incremental migration plan rather than trying to move everything at once.​.

Industry observers note that ​I think about modernization as four steps, and each one becomes a layer of the platform you end up with. First, unify the isolated systems in an open lakehouse built on object storage and open table formats such as Iceberg or Delta, holding one governed copy of structured and unstructured data. Feed it through streaming and change data capture, because agents need current information, not last night’s batch.

Sources indicate that second, define shared business definitions in a semantic layer, so “revenue” or “customer” means the same thing in every system. Third, capture how those entities relate in an ontology and knowledge graph. This is what gives an agent the context for its decisions. Fourth, put governed retrieval across structured and unstructured data, with governance as code providing access management, lineage and a replayable audit trail. Agents also need their own identities with least-privilege access, and cost controls belong in the design from the start, because the cost of running models decides what is affordable at scale.​.

Recent findings suggest that data trust is crucial, but it’s especially challenging when different teams have different standards for what good data looks like. Trust is an interface problem you engineer: one definition, enforced in the pipeline.

One useful mechanism is a data contract, a machine-readable agreement covering schema, quality requirements and service-level expectations between producer and consumer. It functions like a stable API, making the relationship between those parties more predictable.

​Another is shift-left governance. Instead of checking lineage, quality and policy at the review end of a process, organizations should embed those requirements as code where data is produced. Privacy, risk and compliance rules belong in that code too, with identity and access management deciding which people and agents can see each dataset.​.

It has been revealed that many current operating systems and data warehouses were built to answer yesterday’s question for a human. An agent-ready platform has to serve decisions to a machine in real time, with context, semantics and governance built into its design. That is what matters most as we design the next generation of data platform architecture.​.

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

A merger between Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -5.65%) and Tesla (TSLA -0.20%) would have far-reaching consequences, not least by combining a leader in physical artificial intelligence (AI) -- Tesla's electric vehicles, robotaxi, and Optimus robots -- with a organization that has a rapidly growing AI infrastructure services business (SpaceX).

Sources indicate that that combination could have profound consequences for the major near-term catalyst for both companies, namely robotaxi, and that should be considered a threat to Uber Technologies (UBER +0.98%). Here's why.

It has been revealed that to be clear and consistent, I don't think aggressively pursuing a merger is in the best interest of Tesla shareholders right now. In truth, we don't know if a bid will occur and what the terms will be. However, it strikes me that Tesla shareholders have waited for years and endured plenty of missed robotaxi timelines, the disappointments of Cybertruck, and industrywide downward revisions to electric vehicle sales, only to sell out just as Tesla is set to scale up its robotaxi rollout.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

That's an issue for Tesla shareholders, as they could end up with a larger share of the latest manufacturer than the 47% ownership stake Bank of America analysts estimated in an all-stock deal. Still, I think there's another group of shareholders who should be more worried: Uber shareholders.

A merger would create even better conditions for Tesla to realize its ambition to become a transportation-as-a-service (TaaS) company running a fleet of low-cost-per-mile Cybercabs. That's a direct threat to Uber's marketplace, at least in the areas where Cybercab has regulatory clearance. The threat has not gone unnoticed, and there's a reason Uber already has multi-partner autonomous robotaxi arrangements with companies like Waymo, Zoox, and Wayve.

When Tesla CEO Elon Musk states the "vast majority" of Cybercab will be "Tesla-owned and Transport-as-a-Service," this is highly unlikely to encompass a partnership with Uber.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

In addition, merging with SpaceX would bring many benefits for Tesla's robotaxi.

In a recent development, all told, everything points to a merger making it easier for Tesla to ramp robotaxi and drive Cybercab's total cost of ownership (TCO) per mile lower. The latter is the key metric to follow, as it would facilitate a virtuous cycle in which low ride fares encourage further Cybercab fleet expansion. That's a real risk for Uber, because if its robotaxi partners can't achieve a comparable TCO, then Tesla's robotaxi could make significant inroads into some of its most profitable geographies.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
  • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
  • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” remarked head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

Industry observers note that A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a major cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

Industry observers note that he lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Recent findings suggest that vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

According to recent reports, bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that major-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his fresh-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on latest players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

Sources indicate that his team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the substantial spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s upcoming leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

Industry observers note that de Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

According to recent reports, spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

According to recent reports, brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews noted: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

It has been revealed that “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

For the full year, our revenue increased nearly 40% to more than $15 billion, with robust double-digit growth across all of our end markets. AI infrastructure-driven investments drove significant growth for both our ATE and Data Center businesses. That noted, more than two-thirds of our total growth was driven by non-AI-centric markets, highlighting the diversity of our customer base and our ability to capitalize on numerous secular tailwinds, as well as the broader cyclical recovery.

Our fiscal 2026 top-line growth was paired with significant margin expansion, which enabled us to deliver record free cash flow of $5.5 billion. We attribute these results to the optionality and resiliency of our business model, long-term commitment to innovation and customer success, and strong operational execution right across the firm. As our customers tackle ever more difficult challenges at the boundary between the physical and digital worlds, we believe we are well-positioned to deliver and capture even greater value in the future. As we have long said, R&D is our first call on capital because innovation is the wellspring of ADI's value creation.

Sources indicate that our R&D investments in fiscal 2026 were the largest in our history, spanning analog, digital, software, and AI. We also continued ramping investments to enhance our customers' end-to-end experience of ADI from ideation to realization. On the M&A side, our acquisition of Alif added AI-native microcontrollers and fusion processors to our AI toolbox. In addition, our acquisition of Empower strengthens our ability to grow the core power market, which we view as one of the largest SAM opportunities within AI infrastructure. Taken together, these investments significantly expanded our ability to solve increasingly complex challenges for our customers, delivering more complete solutions, combining cutting-edge sensing, signal processing, connectivity, and power.

Recent findings suggest that we credit this overall investment strategy for our record design and pipeline growth of 40% this past year, eclipsing our FY 2025 record, with contributions across all end markets and regions. Our robust customer pipeline is more than a leading indicator of future revenue, however. We believe it reflects the growing criticality of our solutions in the AI era, as rapid technological evolution creates ever more complex challenges across numerous and different markets. Customers are increasingly turning to ADI's higher-value offerings to help lower their total cost of ownership, accelerate their time to market, and, of course, enhance system performance. Our differentiated value is reflected in ADI's average selling prices, which are more than 4x the industry average.

The ASPs of our newer products are notably higher, reflecting the increasing value of our solutions that we are delivering to our customers. I would like to spend the remainder of my planned remarks sharing how we are translating innovation into growth for ADI across the various market sectors, beginning with our industrial business, which comprises test and measurement, automation, aerospace and defense, healthcare, and energy. Starting first, test and measurement. We are benefiting from the intensely demanding test requirements of modern AI compute, memory, networking, and power systems, where complexity is increasing at an extraordinary rate. This plays directly to ADI's leadership in high-performance signal intelligence that transforms raw physics into insight and response.

The greater accuracy, bandwidth, and measurement precision enabled by our technology helps customers test next-generation devices more rapidly, more efficiently, and with greater confidence. This resulted in record ATE and ETM revenue this year, and record design-ins that we believe position us for continued growth through fiscal 2027 and beyond. In industrial automation, customers continue to digitalize, automate, and deploy robots across semiconductor fabs, biopharma, data centers, and other manufacturing environments to accelerate productivity and address evolving geopolitical and labor dynamics. As a result, our automation revenue and design-ins across industrial control, connectivity, and robotics segments accelerated significantly in fiscal 2026, with the fastest growth coming from robotics.

It has been revealed that we expect the next evolution of robotics from automation to autonomy will unlock tasks that historically required human intervention and create opportunity for higher-value ADI content and subsystems that can reduce latency and increase system accuracy. Autonomous robotic modalities, including humanoids, which can require up to 10x more ADI content compared to traditional robots, will steadily increase our opportunity over time. In aerospace and defense, systems are evolving rapidly to sense threats earlier, communicate securely in contested environments, and make mission-critical decisions much, much faster. These requirements are driving increasingly complex radar, communications, and autonomous machines, where ADI's ability to combine RF, signal processing, IMUs, and power management into higher-value solutions is differentiated.

In this sector, we almost doubled growth in our design pipeline this past year across both established and emerging defense customers, which we believe positions us for continued growth in 2027 and beyond. In healthcare, our revenue growth accelerated in 2026 as innovation across the industry increasingly converged around continuous glucose monitoring, AI-assisted imaging, and surgical robotics. Our precision sensing, signal processing, algorithms, and ultra-low-power technologies are helping customers to deliver innovative solutions designed to better manage chronic disease, help clinicians detect and diagnose conditions earlier, and make complex procedures more precise and less invasive. Our growing design and pipeline across myriad applications there positions ADI for continued growth in fiscal 2027 and reinforces the potential of our longer-term opportunity.

In energy, rapidly rising electricity demand is magnifying one of the world's most fundamental engineering challenges: how to generate, manage, store, and deliver significantly more power while improving efficiency and reliability. ADI sits at several key points across that system. For example, our precision sensing enables greater visibility and control of the grid, while our battery management technologies enable more efficient storage and local distribution. Energy was one of our strongest areas of pipeline growth through fiscal 2026, reinforcing our long-term outlook for this business. Turning now to automotive, we delivered a second consecutive year of record revenue, despite lower vehicle production, due to our strong and expanding position in next-generation ADAS and infotainment systems.

Sources indicate that as vehicles move toward greater autonomy, they must process dramatically more sensor information, move more data, and reliably power many interconnected subsystems, all the while meeting demanding requirements for signal integrity, energy efficiency, and safety. These challenges play to ADI's strengths in high-speed connectivity and power solutions designed to support functional safety requirements. L2+ autonomous driving systems remain relatively early in their global adoption, and as the industry progresses toward higher levels of autonomy, we expect content opportunities for ADI to continue to increase. In the past year, design and growth across our GMSL, A2B, and functionally safe power solutions underscores our substantial role in enabling the vehicle of tomorrow.

We saw a strong increase in designs for battery management solutions, which we expect to grow in the coming year and beyond as EV adoption increases. Not surprisingly, our data center business was our fastest-growing market in fiscal 2026, both from a revenue and design-in perspective. Robust investments in AI infrastructure are creating enormous challenges around two of the physical bottlenecks to scaling AI: moving exponentially more data and efficiently delivering unprecedented power loads. ADI is well-positioned to address both. In the networking domain, our optical control technology keeps electro-optical systems precisely tuned across everything from pluggables to OCS, so that every packet of light is accurate, stable, and efficient.

As you know, data center power has become one of the most significant constraints to AI advancement, as increasing rack and processor densities are fundamentally changing how power is converted, controlled, protected, and delivered. Customers are choosing ADI to help ensure that every watt used in the data center is available for computation and maximum impact. As the resulting thermodynamic challenges grow with increasing power density, liquid cooling is shifting from an option to a requirement. Customers are turning to ADI to translate physical signals, such as temperature, flow, leakage, and coolant health, into actionable intelligence, which is creating a new differentiated content opportunity.

Overall, we believe our data center revenues will continue to be one of the faster-growing businesses in 2027 and beyond. Finally, continued demand at the premium end of the consumer market overcame memory headwinds to drive double-digit growth in revenue and design activity across premium handsets, wearables, hearables, and gaming segments, which positions ADI for continued diversified growth in this sector in 2027 and beyond. In closing, FY 2026 demonstrated what makes ADI different. We are built to define and capture new waves of opportunity as we compound the businesses underpinning our resilience through cycles.

Industry observers note that we leverage a six-decade culture of curiosity and cutting-edge innovation to continuously advance the state of the art at the electrophysical interface, a boundary that is increasingly central to the advance of technology's most valuable applications. Our customers increasingly choose ADI as a strategic partner for our applications, domain expertise, scope of high-performance analog software and AI capabilities, and differentiated hybrid manufacturing strategy. As we enter 2027, we continue to invest with discipline to further enhance and extend the value we can deliver to our customers and shareholders alike in the years ahead. With that, I'll turn it over to Rich.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Sources indicate that health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The manufacturer also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

Sources indicate that the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Sources indicate that furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

In a recent development, social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it introduces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

Industry observers note that heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

In a recent development, specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active customers in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," remarked the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the firm's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

Recent findings suggest that the five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

According to recent reports, while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the tech giant raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

It has been revealed that svanberg stated that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.
