Industry observers note that abercrombie (ANF +19.69%) reported third quarter results reflecting its 16th consecutive quarter of sales growth, with management citing balanced performance across both brand families and all three geographic regions. The company stated that it is executing on strategic priorities including brand expansion, gross margin stabilization, and technological investment. Management reported that strong cash flow enabled continued share repurchases and reinvestment in the store fleet, with the company remaining on track for its fourth consecutive year of net sales growth.

Sources indicate that operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Abercrombie & Fitch Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Earnings Call. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker, Mo Gupta, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Mohit (Mo) Gupta: Thank you. Good morning, and welcome to our Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Joining me today on the call are Fran Horowitz, Chief Executive Officer; Scott Lipesky, Chief Operating Officer; and Robert J. Ball, Chief Financial Officer. Earlier this morning, we issued our third quarter earnings release, which is available on our website at corporate.abercrombie.com under the Investors section. Also available on our website is an investor presentation. Please keep in mind that we will make certain forward-looking statements on the call.

These statements are subject to the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from the expectations and assumptions we mentioned today. These factors and uncertainties are discussed in our reports and filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. In addition, we'll be referring to certain non-GAAP financial measures during the call. Additional details and reconciliations of GAAP to adjusted non-GAAP financial measures are included in the release and the investor presentation issued earlier this morning. With that, I will turn the call over to Fran.

Fran Horowitz: Thanks, Mo, and thanks, everyone, for joining. I'm pleased to report another strong quarter for our business. Net sales grew 11% to a third quarter record of $1.4 billion, ahead of our expectations and our 16th consecutive quarter of growth. We've grown the business each quarter for 4 years running, and that momentum continues. You've heard me emphasize the importance of balance, and we highlighted it again this quarter. All 3 regions and both brands delivered double-digit net sales growth with each seeing growth rate accelerate from second quarter levels. The strong top line, coupled with disciplined inventory management, enabled us to deliver healthy sales growth with higher AUR and lower promotions.

Recent findings suggest that this performance flowed to the bottom line, where we delivered an operating margin of 15.5%, nicely above our expectations. And we continue to execute against our capital allocation priorities, investing in marketing, stores, digital and technology, all to support long-term growth while increasing net income per diluted share 62% year-over-year to $3.82. We also used our balance sheet to repurchase $100 million of shares in the quarter, bringing our year-to-date total to $382 million or 9% of shares outstanding at the beginning of the year. This marked our 11th straight quarter of share repurchases. Our teams continue to deliver for customers around the world, and we entered the important holiday season with momentum across brands and regions.

With that strong performance, we are raising our full year net sales and earnings expectations. We continue to expect fiscal 2026 to mark our fourth consecutive full year of net sales growth with consistent strong double-digit operating margins and significant cash return to shareholders through share repurchases. Turning back to the quarter. All 3 regions delivered double-digit net sales growth. The Americas grew 11% with stable traffic trends as we moved from back-to-school into fall. EMEA delivered 12% net sales growth with comparable sales up 4%, a significant sequential improvement from the second quarter. Germany performance improved nicely as the team continued to dial in marketing, promotions and inventory to customer traffic and demand.

According to recent reports, several other European markets returned to growth on healthy conversion trends, and the U.K. continues to be a consistent growth market. APAC performed ahead of our expectations again this quarter, growing 24% on strong traffic, particularly in stores. While still evaluating the right go-to-market strategies in the APAC region, the team has continued to invest in marketing and manage inventory, and we've seen stronger top line performance, especially in Hollister. Diving further into the brands, Hollister had a great back-to-school season to start the quarter and carried that momentum throughout, delivering 11% net sales growth on top of 16% growth and record third quarter sales last year.

Recent findings suggest that as we discussed last quarter, the team prioritized receipts heading into back-to-school to support customer demand, and we continue to Read & React as the season progressed. That discipline allowed us to keep inventory tight, reduce promotional levels and deliver higher AUR. Growth was balanced across men's and women's with fleece, knits, graphics and bottoms performing well. Hollister's denim campaign with rising star Freya Skye drove strong social engagement and positive fan response to events in both the U.S. and U.K., demonstrating the power of connecting with our customers with culturally relevant talent and experiences.

Industry observers note that following a strong third quarter, Hollister is bringing an exciting flow of newness throughout the holiday season, including new product drops at Target as our continued partnership gives us another way to reach new and existing customers. In our owned and operated stores, we've invested to ensure our customers have the latest brand experience. Year-to-date, we've opened 23 new stores and remodeled or rightsized 48 Hollister stores, a substantial portion of our fleet. Overall, Hollister has made considerable progress, and we're excited for what the brand can do to cap off 2026. At Abercrombie brands, we had an excellent transition into fall with net sales growing 12% and accelerating nicely from the second quarter.

It has been revealed that inventory remained tightly managed and strong product acceptance allowed us to deliver improved AUR and lower-than-expected promotions. Growth was balanced across men's and women's and across tops and bottoms. Women's knits and sweaters performed particularly well, while men's saw strength across jeans and pants. Our active assortment under Your Personal Best continues to perform well. We recently showcased YPB through a partnership with Barry's, the fast-growing global fitness brand, bringing a collection of studio-ready activewear to its highly engaged community through Barry's studios and our direct channels. Abercrombie's momentum extends to our store fleet, an integral part of how customers experience the brand.

Our A&F SoHo store has continued to exceed expectations since opening in July with YPB, footwear and accessories all part of the experience. We've already brought elements of that modern A&F expression to 15 stores in major markets just in time for holiday. We're midway through another successful season with the NFL, connecting with fans in more ways across product, partnerships and experiences. As an official fashion partner of the NFL, the Dallas Cowboys and Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, we're engaging fans at game time events and offering our NFL assortment at select stadiums and on nflshop.com. And in time for holiday, we recently launched a collection co-designed with Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb.

The NFL assortment also extends to abercrombie kids with styles for boys and girls. As we move into the holiday season, we're offering a new digital gift card on the Abercrombie app and website, featuring ideas for every age from babies and toddlers to massive kids and adults. Creating memorable holiday experiences has been part of Abercrombie for more than 130 years, and we're building on that heritage in new and relevant ways as we look to finish the year strong. In addition to our strong quarterly results, we've made meaningful progress against our 4 priorities for the year.

According to recent reports, that includes growing our brands and owned and operated business while adding fresh avenues of growth, stabilizing gross margins against external cost pressures, investing in tools and technologies like AI to improve speed and efficiency and maintaining strong profitability to fuel excess cash return to shareholders through share repurchases. On that first priority, our growth continues to start with the customer, a consistent focus that has resulted in net sales growth every quarter for 4 consecutive years. Our teams have stayed close throughout the year, testing, learning and evolving our assortments alongside engaging marketing across brands and regions.

According to recent reports, we've invested meaningfully in stores and digital to improve the customer experience while partnerships and newly introduced product categories are helping us reach new customers. While early, it's really encouraging to see how our evolved model is driving brand love, awareness and consideration even in well-established markets like the U.S. It's also exciting to see how we can make this much progress on global brand growth, including new partnerships and categories for our brands while still balancing our other 3 business priorities. We've been able to manage inventory and control promotions by focusing on giving the customer the fashion and fit they value, which has enabled gross margin improvement despite freight cost pressure.

In a recent development, we've continued to invest in our digital systems and infrastructure, including deploying AI-based solutions across the customer journey, which we believe is critical to brand health and relevance. And of course, with our strong culture of financial discipline, we've been able to keep our double-digit operating margins and also repurchased 9% of shares outstanding year-to-date. Three quarters in, 2026 has been a year of consistent profitable growth. That momentum, along with a strong start to November, has led us to increase our full year sales and profitability outlook.

We now expect to deliver our fourth consecutive year of net sales growth, another year of strong double-digit operating margins and growth in net income per diluted share while maintaining our target of returning at least $500 million to shareholders through share repurchases. The consistency of our results reflects the strength of our operating model, the health of our global brands and the financial discipline of this team. To our associates around the world, thank you for everything you do to deliver for our customers every day. I'm incredibly proud of what we continue to accomplish together. We're ready for holiday and a strong finish to 2026, and we look forward to updating you all on both in early March.

And with that, I'll hand it over to Robert.

Robert J. Ball: Thanks, Fran, and good morning, everyone. I'd also like to thank our teams around the world for another strong quarter and the work they've done to position us for the holiday season. We delivered record third quarter net sales of $1.44 billion, up 11% year-over-year and above the 5% to 6% growth range we provided in August. Comparable sales increased 6% and AUR grew high single digits, supported by lower promotional activity, driving better-than-expected results to our outlook. We're particularly encouraged by the quality and balance of that growth. Both brands in all 3 regions delivered double-digit net sales growth with sequential acceleration across the business. Starting with our regions.

Recent findings suggest that net sales increased 11% in the Americas, 12% in EMEA and 24% in APAC. Comparable sales increased 5% in the Americas, 4% in EMEA and 24% in APAC. By brand, Abercrombie brands net sales increased 12% with comparable sales up 6%. Hollister delivered 11% net sales growth against last year's record with comparable sales up 5%. Both brands grew net sales across all 3 regions. Across regions and brands, the spread between net sales growth and comparable sales was driven by net latest stores and third-party channel performance. Importantly, we're seeing contributions from multiple sources of growth. Our existing direct-to-consumer business continues to perform, while the new stores and third-party distribution partnerships are providing incremental opportunities to reach customers.

According to recent reports, that combination is encouraging as we think about the durability of our growth. Turning to profitability. Third quarter operating income was $223 million, and operating margin was 15.5% of sales, above the 13% to 14% outlook we provided in August. Our results included approximately $20 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, contributing around 150 basis points to operating margin, consistent with our outlook. But importantly, the underlying business also performed ahead of our expectations. At the midpoint of our outlook, operating margin exceeded expectations by approximately 200 basis points, driven primarily by stronger gross margin performance from higher AUR with additional benefit from expense leverage. Year-over-year, operating margin increased approximately 350 basis points from 12% in the third quarter of 2025.

Of that improvement, approximately 150 basis points came from tariff refunds and approximately 80 basis points came from lower year-over-year tariff expense on products sold in the quarter. Higher Q3 AUR was mostly offset by higher freight, so the remaining approximately 100 basis points of operating margin improvement came from operating expense leverage, particularly from marketing and fulfillment and selling expense. We're encouraged by our operating margin performance. Higher AUR and disciplined promotional activity are supporting gross margins, while continued expense management is allowing us to invest in the business and maintain strong profitability. And importantly, we're delivering that performance while continuing to make investments in stores, digital capabilities and the infrastructure needed to support future growth.

According to recent reports, moving below operating income. Our tax rate for the quarter was 29%, better than expected, primarily due to stronger international performance. Net income per diluted share was $3.82 compared with diluted earnings per share of $2.36 last year and above our outlook of $2.90 to $3.20. Both our third quarter outlook and results include approximately $0.40 per share of benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. We do not right now anticipate any additional IEEPA tariff refunds, and we updated the table in the press release and investor presentation with additional detail on the timing of tariff refunds and ongoing tariff expense. Turning to inventory and the balance sheet.

According to recent reports, ending inventory at cost increased around 4% year-over-year with units up mid-single digits and aligned with our expectations for unit sales growth. We believe inventory remains appropriately positioned as we enter the holiday season, giving our teams flexibility to respond to consumer demand while maintaining promotional discipline. On the balance sheet, we ended the quarter with $724 million of cash and cash equivalents and approximately $1.2 billion of liquidity. During the quarter, we repurchased $100 million worth of shares, bringing year-to-date repurchases to $382 million and our 11th consecutive quarter of share repurchases. Year-to-date, that represents approximately 9% of beginning of year shares outstanding. We ended the quarter with $468 million remaining on our current repurchase authorization.

According to recent reports, our approach to capital allocation remains consistent. We're investing in the business to support profitable growth, maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning excess cash to shareholders. Turning to the outlook. Our strong third quarter performance and expectations for higher fourth quarter demand support an increase to our full year sales and EPS outlook. As a reminder, our full year outlook includes the entire $120 million of tariff refunds recognized during the second and third quarters. We estimate that the refund will contribute approximately 220 basis points to full year operating margin and approximately $2.15 to full year diluted earnings per share.

Separate from the refunds, our outlook continues to reflect current Section 301 tariff rates of 10% to 12.5% effective on global imports into the U.S. Based on those assumptions, we continue to expect approximately 10 basis points of year-over-year gross margin favorability from lower year-over-year tariff expense on sold product, which we expect to be more than offset by higher freight costs. For the full year, we now expect net sales growth of around 6% from the $5.27 billion in 2025, with growth across regions and brands. We now expect mid-single-digit AUR improvement for the full year and approximately 20 basis points of benefit to net sales from foreign currency.

Industry observers note that we continue to expect full year operating margin in the range of 14.5% to 15%, including approximately 220 basis points of benefit from the IEEPA tariff refunds. We're forecasting a tax rate around 28%, diluted weighted average shares of around 44 million and net income per diluted share in the range of $13.70 to $13.90. The EPS outlook includes an estimated $2.15 from IEEPA tariff refunds. For capital allocation, we expect capital expenditures around $260 million. We remain on track to deliver approximately 130 fresh store experiences, including 50 new stores and 80 remodels and rightsizes against approximately 20 closures.

These investments remain an notable part of our growth strategy, allowing us to expand our reach while improving productivity and customer experience of our existing fleet. We continue to expect at least $500 million of share repurchases for 2026. For the fourth quarter of 2026, we expect net sales growth of around 7% from the Q4 2025 level of $1.67 billion with growth across regions and brands. We expect a fourth quarter operating margin around 15%, a modest expansion from the fourth quarter of 2025. This is largely in line with our prior outlook, but has been updated to reflect some incremental freight expense of around 100 basis points.

Despite the increase in freight, we continue to expect modest gross margin improvement year-over-year, partially offset by modest expense deleverage, mainly from incentive compensation. We expect a fourth quarter tax rate of around 28% and net income per diluted share in the range of $4.40 to $4.60. Diluted weighted average shares are expected to be around 43 million, including the anticipated impact of at least $120 million of fourth quarter share repurchases. To close, we are pleased with our third quarter results and the consistency of execution we've delivered throughout 2026. We've now delivered 16 consecutive quarters of sales growth, and we're doing it while maintaining strong profitability, investing in the business and returning significant capital to shareholders.

What gives us conviction in our model isn't just our performance in any single quarter, but it's also our consistency. We're seeing healthy, sustained growth across our core business, expanding our reach through latest stores and partnerships and maintaining the financial discipline needed to support both. As we look ahead, we're focused on adding to this track record while investing in the opportunities that can drive our next chapter of growth. We believe that we're well positioned to finish 2026 strong and carry that momentum into 2027, and we look forward to covering both in early March. With that, operator, we're ready for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question will be coming from the line of Dana Lauren Telsey of Telsey Advisory Group.

Anything you saw there? And any distinction in trends between women's and men's? And lastly, just following up on the freight costs. How much of a headwind do you see that going forward? So we saw growth across brands, regions, genders, channels, really, really terrific with improved AUR and a strong bottom line. From an AUR perspective, if you think of the walk back from like that Q3 to Q4 walk again, planning to deliver high single-digit AUR growth in Q3, planning for, call it, mid-singles AUR on the full year, and that kind of works out to kind of mid-single-digit growth here in Q4. So promotions are not expecting any sort of meaningful promotion pullback year-over-year, but like we do every quarter, we'll come in day by day and see if we can pull back on the promo here, depth of a discount there and see if we can get some margin growth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The manufacturer has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the organization's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

It has been revealed that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

Sources indicate that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

Kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the manufacturer to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

"As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

According to recent reports, moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production firm with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent confirmed an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

Heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from fresh shares.

"CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," noted Richardson.

It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable company, regardless of market conditions.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

Sources indicate that hecla Mining (HL -2.68%), a silver and gold miner, closed at $10.90, down 2.7%. Silver miners were under pressure in premarket trading after silver prices fell on rate-hike concerns, and investors are watching metal prices and upcoming management commentary.Trading volume reached 48.6M shares, coming in about 5% above its three-month average of 32.3M shares.

S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) fell 0.5% to 7,201.09, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) dropped 1.5% to 23,73.54. Among silver and gold mining peers, Pan American Silver (PAAS -3.87%) closed at $31.07, down 3.9%, and Coeur Mining (CDE -2.27%) finished at $11.19, down 2.3%.

Hecla Mining's stock, like other precious metal mining companies, is sensitive to commodity prices and interest rates. Naturally, higher commodity prices typically translate into increased revenue. However, interest rates also feed into commodity prices.

Typically, they move in opposite directions. That's because they become less attractive as interest rates move higher since physical commodities don't earn anything. Holding other assets, such as bonds or dividend-paying stocks, becomes more attractive in higher-interest rate environments.

Industry observers note that earlier this month, Hecla Mining reported third-quarter results. Sales grew more than 18% from the second quarter to $394.8 million. Management provided guidance on production and costs, but investors will likely focus on macroeconomic challenges that affect commodity prices until the next quarterly earnings release.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE -16.31%) led that decline.
  • It has been revealed that dell's earnings release for the quarter ended Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:54PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Dell Technologies ›.

Industry observers note that dell Technologies (DELL -11.83%) shares rose about 3% to $305 in after-hours trading Tuesday after the company reported that quarterly revenue more than doubled and raised its full-year forecast. The stock had closed at $295.28 in the regular session, down 12% from Monday's $334.91, as AI hardware shares sold off.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE -16.31%) led that decline. Its shares fell about 16% after executives said on Monday's earnings call that memory and other components could stay scarce through at least the second half of 2028. HPE also guided for its cloud and AI business to keep about 14% of sales as operating profit in fiscal 2027, down from 18.4% in the quarter it just reported. Dell, which sells many of the same servers, fell with it.

It has been revealed that dell's earnings release for the quarter ended Oct. 30 indicated revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. And adjusted earnings rose 265% to $9.45 per share, well above the $6.59 analysts expected.

Recent findings suggest that most of the growth came from the Infrastructure Solutions Group, which sells servers, networking, and storage. Its revenue tripled to $42.0 billion. AI-optimized server sales rose 291% to $22.0 billion, and traditional servers and networking rose 235% to $15.0 billion. "We are now a different company," Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke noted in the release.

Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI orders in the quarter and ended it with a record AI backlog of $132.3 billion, about two-thirds of the revenue it expects for the whole year.

Gross margin was 21% of revenue, up from 20.7% a year earlier. Helping to drive that increase, the infrastructure business kept 17% of its sales as operating profit, compared with 12.4% a year ago, and its operating income quadrupled to $7.1 billion.

Lower spending also helped. Operating expenses fell to 7.5% of revenue from 12.9%, and Chief Financial Officer David Kennedy remarked that is driving "higher profitability, even as AI servers become a larger part of our business." AI servers tend to carry thinner margins than storage, so a rising AI share usually pulls margins down, but this quarter it clearly didn't.

According to recent reports, on the other hand, PCs were the weak spot. The Client Solutions Group grew revenue by 3% to $12.9 billion, consumer sales fell by 15%, and the segment's operating income slipped by 6% to $704 million.

Dell raised its full-year revenue forecast by $10 billion to $202 billion, up 78% from last year, and its AI server sales forecast to $78 billion from $74 billion. It now expects adjusted earnings of $29.68 per share, up from $25.50. For the fourth quarter, it guided revenue to $56.3 billion and adjusted earnings to $8.40 per share.

Industry observers note that separately, the company returned a record $4.9 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends in the quarter, and its board approved an additional $25 billion in repurchases. Free cash flow rose to $3.5 billion from $506 million a year earlier.

Recent findings suggest that inventories rose to $29.4 billion on Oct. 30 from $10.4 billion at the end of January, and total debt rose to $37.7 billion from $31.5 billion. If component costs keep climbing, as HPE expects, Dell may need to keep raising prices, and one quarter of higher margins doesn't show it can do that indefinitely.

The stock is also volatile. It rose about 20% on Monday after Nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, then gave back most of that gain on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, even after Tuesday's after-hours gain, the stock trades at about 10 times the adjusted earnings Dell expects for the fiscal year ending in January. That's a low multiple for a organization whose revenue just doubled and whose backlog covers much of next year. And while the stock fell on worries about a rival's margins, Dell's own margins rose.

The case depends on AI spending holding up, the same bet behind most AI stocks. Investors who already own plenty of semiconductor stocks and other AI infrastructure names should know Dell adds to that exposure rather than diversifying it. Those who want to see whether component costs hit margins can wait for next quarter's report.

Wall Street's $1.4 Trillion Bubble May Be on the Verge of Bursting -- but It's Not Artificial Intelligence (AI)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the past four years, euphoria for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has fueled a historic rally in the stock market.
  • According to recent reports, although much of Wall Street's attention is focused on whether AI stocks are overvalued, another vulnerability is lurking in the background.
  • Let's explore why margin debt represents one of Wall Street's biggest threats and what smart investors can do about it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adam Spatacco – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

Over the past four years, euphoria for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has fueled a historic rally in the stock market. Enthusiasm surrounding AI infrastructure and software has helped propel the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.50%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -1.48%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.85%) to record highs.

According to recent reports, although much of Wall Street's attention is focused on whether AI stocks are overvalued, another vulnerability is lurking in the background. Investors are borrowing unprecedented sums of money to participate in the stock market's ongoing rally. This introduces another layer of risk into an already frothy market.

Let's explore why margin debt represents one of Wall Street's biggest threats and what smart investors can do about it.

Margin debt is a financial term used to describe money investors borrow from a brokerage firm to buy stocks. This practice is more commonly known as leverage. It allows investors to increase their purchasing power without committing an equivalent amount of their own capital up front.

Recent findings suggest that although borrowing can be lucrative when stocks are rising, leverage works in both directions. For example, imagine you have $10,000 and borrow another $10,000 from a brokerage firm. With $20,000 invested, a 25% increase in the portfolio's value generates a $5,000 gain. This represents a 50% return on your original capital. However, if the portfolio declines by 25%, you would lose $5,000, or half of your original investment. A 50% decline effectively wipes out your original capital.

Sources indicate that according to data compiled by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), margin debt reached a record $1.5 trillion in June. To appreciate the magnitude of that figure, let's take a look at borrowing levels during other periods of unusually high speculation in the stock market.

Although today's borrowing levels dwarf the historical figures in terms of absolute dollars, it's important to consider the fact that the stock market has become considerably larger. Nevertheless, the rapid accumulation of debt over the last year or so suggests investors are developing more of an appetite for risk.

According to recent reports, one of the most dangerous aspects of using leverage is that investors do not necessarily control when their positions are sold. Brokerage firms require investors to maintain a minimum level of liquidity in their margin accounts. If declining stock prices cause an account to fall below that threshold, investors could face a margin call. This would require them to deposit additional collateral or reduce their positions.

Brokerages also have the authority to liquidate positions without obtaining an investor's permission. When this happens across several accounts at the same time, the forced selling puts additional downward pressure on stock prices. As a result, more margin calls are triggered, and a destructive cycle is created.

With all of that remarked, current margin debt levels could suggest investors are moderating their risk exposure. At the end of October, margin debt was recorded at $1.4 trillion, or about 3.6% below its peak from June. While this could indicate investors are becoming more cautious, declining balances can also reflect forced liquidations rather than voluntary reductions in risk.

Recent findings suggest that it's notable to understand that elevated margin debt doesn't necessarily mean a stock market crash is imminent. Borrowing often increases alongside rising stock prices. Ultimately, margin debt is better viewed as a potential amplifier of market volatility rather than a reliable predictor of when a crash or drawdown will occur.

Even if excessive leverage contributes to a pullback, smart investors should remember that the stock market always demonstrates resilience. The S&P 500 declined by 49% following the dot-com bubble and nearly 57% during the financial crisis. More recently, the index fell 34% during the COVID-19 crash and 25% during the 2022 bear market. Despite these setbacks -- depicted by the grey columns in the chart below -- the S&P 500 eventually recovered and reached fresh record highs.

The takeaway here is that investors who buy stocks using their own capital wind up having more financial flexibility to endure prolonged downturns than those whose brokerage firms can force them to sell at unfavorable prices.

Although nobody knows whether today's borrowing levels will culminate in another stock market bubble bursting event, history suggests that staying diversified and remaining invested through volatility is a more prudent approach to building long-term wealth than attempting to predict the next market crash.

By Neil Patel – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:10PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

It has been revealed that sizable down cycles aren't upcoming to the Netflix (NFLX +1.32%) story. The latest dip, with shares down 56% from their peak (as of Nov. 23), is certainly troubling for investors to witness. But it's smaller than the 76% drop in 2022 and the 79% fall before that in 2011.

Sources indicate that history notes that the streaming stock has always made a comeback. And despite the most recent tumble, the shares have still returned 392% in the past 10 years. Getting in early on a true disruptor usually produces this type of performance.

Is it time to buy Netflix for $1,000? At the current price of $58.10, investors can add about 17 shares to their portfolios.

Sources indicate that netflix's economic moat comes from its scale. With more than 325 million paid memberships, it spreads its content budget across a far bigger audience than any rival can. That's a powerful cost advantage. Netflix is targeting a 31.5% operating margin in 2026. Walt Disney's (DIS +1.86%) non-sports streaming segment, which includes Disney+ and Hulu, posted an 11.5% margin in its latest fiscal year.

And the runway is still long if you ask the leadership team. Chief Financial Officer Spence Neumann said in July that Netflix was "under 45% penetrated into addressable households around the world." It also captures 5% of TV viewing time and only about 7% of its addressable revenue opportunity.

It has been revealed that the bottom line keeps improving. Operating margin expanded from 26.7% in 2024 to 29.5% in 2025 and is projected at 31.5% this year, as noted. Free cash flow is also expected to reach roughly $12 billion in 2026, compared to $9.5 billion last year. Growth is translating into serious profits.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

According to recent reports, so why has Netflix stock gotten clobbered? Growth is slowing. Revenue increased 16.2% year over year in Q1 2026, 13.4% in Q2, and 11.8% in Q3. Wall Street expects 11.6% in the fourth quarter.

Recent findings suggest that engagement is a worry, too. View hours rose only 2% in the first half of 2026. Investors also didn't like management's decision to report that figure once a year, starting in 2027, instead of twice.

But all this pessimism has reset the valuation. The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is now 15.1. That's cheaper than the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.50%). Shareholders aren't used to seeing Netflix shares on the discount rack.

At this multiple, Netflix looks like an interesting buy with $1,000. Just don't expect a smooth ride. The stock could move with heightened volatility in the near term. That's why patience is critical.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coca-Cola (KO +1.81%) has increased its dividend for 64 consecutive years.
  • So what could a $10,000 investment in Coca-Cola generate in dividend income over the next decade?
  • 20 closing price of $96.99, a $10,000 investment would purchase around 103.1 shares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jeff Siegel – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:13PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

Coca-Cola (KO +1.81%) has increased its dividend for 64 consecutive years. In February 2026, the beverage giant raised its quarterly payout by roughly 4%, from $0.51 to $0.53 per share. That brings its annual dividend to $2.12 per share.

So what could a $10,000 investment in Coca-Cola generate in dividend income over the next decade?

At Coca-Cola's Nov. 20 closing price of $96.99, a $10,000 investment would purchase around 103.1 shares. With an annual dividend of $2.12 per share, those shares would generate approximately $219 in annual income today, representing a dividend yield of roughly 2.2%.

Sources indicate that but Coca-Cola has a long history of increasing its payout. Assuming the manufacturer continues raising its dividend by 4% annually, its annual dividend could reach $3.14 per share by 2036. That would produce $324 in annual dividend income on the original investment, without purchasing additional shares. And over the entire decade, you would also collect around $2,600 in cumulative dividends.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

It has been revealed that coca-Cola benefits from a portfolio of globally recognized beverage brands, including Sprite, Fanta, and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar. Its established distribution network, recurring consumer demand, and ability to raise prices help support consistent cash generation.

That remarked, the firm faces challenges, including shifting consumer preferences, rising operating costs, and currency fluctuations. And while Coca-Cola's dividend history is impressive, future increases aren't guaranteed.

Recent findings suggest that I wouldn't expect Coca-Cola to deliver explosive growth. At nearly $97 per share, the stock isn't particularly cheap either. But if you're seeking dependable income, Coca-Cola remains an attractive long-term candidate.

My prediction is that a $10,000 investment today could generate approximately $324 in annual dividends by 2036, assuming 4% annual dividend growth and no reinvestment. That's a roughly 48% increase in annual income from the original investment, excluding any potential stock price appreciation. That's not bad.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Sources indicate that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Sources indicate that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Industry observers note that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly notable sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Recent findings suggest that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    #85039. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5247 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
    • The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
    • Recent findings suggest that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

    The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct concerns with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

    Recent findings suggest that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

    Industry observers note that A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

    According to recent reports, joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    According to recent reports, “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca noted, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

    His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

    Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

    Sources indicate that momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

    Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    Recent findings suggest that marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

    According to recent reports, his team indicated an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, upcoming signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

    Sources indicate that they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his upcoming manager.

    Recent findings suggest that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    It has been revealed that city will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “fresh Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

    There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

    In a recent development, of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a fresh season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

    Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

    Recent findings suggest that the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

    It has been revealed that emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

    Industry observers note that manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

    BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

    It has been revealed that maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

    Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    It has been revealed that brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

    In a recent development, pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he mentioned of Guardiola’s grand design.

    In a recent development, tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

    Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s massive idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

    According to recent reports, describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

    After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

    The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

    The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

    Recent findings suggest that no sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for upcoming signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

    Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

    Sources indicate that the Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

    According to recent reports, brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S.
    • Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment.

    Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Industry observers note that this week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The company will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG reveals the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

    Heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    Ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

    According to recent reports, the five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

    "We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," stated Ikeda.

    Ikeda ranks No. 673 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.9%. See Datadog Statistics on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that the next pick, semiconductor giant Nvidia, is also benefiting from AI-driven demand for its products. After attending Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reaffirmed a buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $300, calling it a top pick in the semiconductor space.

    It has been revealed that the five-star analyst said that the conference supported his thesis that Nvidia continues to effectively navigate bottlenecks in the supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding. In fact, Moore is "convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA.".

    While Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the company continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst said that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

    With demand outpacing supply, Moore said that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

    Sources indicate that moore ranks No. 142 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.4%. See Nvidia Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Aerospace company SpaceX recently announced solid third-quarter results, with its AI revenue surging to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the prior-year quarter.

    Sources indicate that impressed by the results, Needham analyst Ryan Koontz reiterated a buy rating on SPCX stock with a price target of $250. Koontz highlighted that SpaceX's Q3 results significantly exceeded expectations, proving that the firm's vertically integrated business model is driving massive scale.

    Furthermore, Koontz emphasized the 195.2% sequential growth in SpaceX's AI revenue, fueled by wholesale spot compute deals. He noted management's increasing focus on its AI strategy, given that it is optimistic about adding 10 gigawatts of incremental capacity during 2027.

    "With increasing confidence on Starship re-use, we meaningfully increase our estimates," said Koontz.

    According to recent reports, koontz ranks No. 357 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 42% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.7%. See SpaceX Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

    Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers. The stock market could remain volatile amid AI trade concerns, macro uncertainties, and geopolitical tensions.

    Industry observers note that in this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income. Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as these experts assign ratings after in-depth financial analysis.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The company reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper declared a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    Following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the firm delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key upgrade was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    Given the recently confirmed base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    Bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the firm's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

    Industry observers note that bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant announced a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Sources indicate that gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the company increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    Gabelman noted that Exxon announced a dividend hike of nearly 4% and aims to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," mentioned the analyst.

    Gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

The company announced a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    Recent findings suggest that in reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier said that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    He noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. In fact, results are tracking toward the higher end of the guidance range, backed by contributions from recently completed projects and the Momentum Midstream deal. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.
